$comment: Generated by mix loka.source_schema from the compiler's source contracts; do not edit.

ActionContribution.description: One source's contribution to an actor's ActionSet (06 §19; ADR-016), applied to the set composed so far by stable action key: union adds the named actions whose keys the set lacks, override adds them and replaces those it has, replace makes the set exactly them, subtract removes them and intersect keeps only them. A key names an engine verb (a registered command type), a cartridge action or a cartridge recipe; union, override and replace take its definition (a cartridge's own over the engine verb's). A room applies its contributions in order after the engine verbs and the cartridge's actions and recipes (kernel/ts/src/actions.ts).

ActionInputParameter.description: An input parameter an action requires (06 §20), one of the ActionInput fields.

Alias.description: A word or phrase a player types to name a detail (21 §6 aliases; 04 §18 aliases) or, for an ActionRecipe, the action (its verb, the first words typed): lowercase letters and digits, the words of a phrase joined by _ (the player's `mooring post` is compared as mooring_post; kernel/ts/src/target.ts gives the normalization). At most 64 characters.

AncestrySpec.description: One authored character choice and its bounded initial effects.

ApiVersion.description: api_version: the authored source document/schema family (05 §3).

AttackProfile.description: Cartridge-owned hit chance and positive damage bounds. Compiler and loader enforce damage_min <= damage_max.

crit.description: Toolbox row G2: a hit whose accuracy roll (the hit draw, uniform in [0, 100)) is below chance is critical and its damage is multiplied by multiplier, before resistances.

BandTable.description: A condition band table (04 §15 as amended 2026-10-02), highest cut first: the band is the first row whose cut p reaches, and maximum = minimum gives the top row. Cuts are strictly descending and the last is 0, so every value has a band, and keys are unique within the table; the compiler reports a table that breaks this as RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID at the table. A pool's bands (ResourceSpec), else the cartridge's world.bands (cartridge.schema.json WorldSettings), else the engine default table.

BandTone.description: A condition band's tone (04 §15 as amended 2026-10-02): how serious the band is; each presenter maps it to its own colour.

BarrierState.description: A barrier's state (21 §5 Barrier: open/closed, locked/unlocked): open, closed (and unlocked) or locked (and closed); a lock needs a closed door, so an open locked barrier does not exist. The legal transitions (04 §5.3 'Lifecycle transition') are closed to open (open), open to closed (close), closed to locked (lock) and locked to closed (unlock); delta.schema.json barrier.transition.

Calendar.description: calendar@1: authored logical units per hour, hours per day, displayed subdivisions, and optional ordered solar/lunar cuts. Cut starts are inclusive; the compiler checks order, cycle bounds and schedule/window hours (lib/loka/content/calendar.ex). Toolbox row 31 adds the season and tide cycles and the weather table (one weighted entry per calendar day, chosen by a hash of the world id and the day).

CalendarCut.description: An inclusive phase start within one authored solar day or lunar period.

CalendarCycle.description: A repeating cycle of ordered cuts in logical time units (lunar; season and tide, toolbox row 31): the phase at time t is the last cut at or before ((t - origin) mod period); the first cut starts at 0.

CapabilityVersion.description: A capability contract version (05 §6): a positive integer. key@version is immutable in meaning once published; a breaking change takes a new version (05 §6, 'Capability version immutability').

CapabilityVersions.description: Exact capability pins, capability key to version (05 §3 requires.capabilities; 05 §6). A map, so one version per key: the canonical decoder rejects a repeated key, and canonical encoding sorts keys.

CartridgeId.description: A cartridge identity (05 §3 id, 05 §4), lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters.

Chapter.description: An ordered chapter marker (mechanics.md Chapters): title is a catalog key; only chapter 0 lacks a story_point, and it has no outcome. Later chapters name a story point and optionally one of its outcome keys (checked at the reference stage).

ClientFeature.description: A presentation/input capability of the installed Loka app (05 §3 client_features), lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters.

CombatSettings.description: Cartridge-owned attack profile, round interval, position multipliers and combat narration keys. Compiler and loader enforce its executable capability and death-setting dependencies.

allies.description: Authored NPCs that fight beside the player (docs/system/mechanics.md, toolbox row 6b, narration ally_hit and ally_miss): the first listed one living in the encounter room strikes the player's target each round, is never an attack target, and its kill credits the player.

target_choice.description: Opts into target choice (docs/system/mechanics.md, toolbox row 6a): during a roster encounter the player's attack on another present active member makes it the primary the player strikes.

CompatibilityRequirements.description: requires (05 §3): a kernel_api range, exact rule_ir and content_schema versions (published cartridges pin them exactly), exact capability versions and required client features. protocol_version is Realm-only and not here (05 §3 'Version vocabulary').

ConditionBand.description: One row of a condition band table: the band key holds when p, the percentage of the pool's range from its minimum, reaches at_percent (in integers: 100 x (current - minimum) >= at_percent x (maximum - minimum)). key is a content Key whose text is band.<key> in the catalog when the cartridge authors it; tone is how serious it is.

Connection.description: One directed exit to another room of the same cartridge (21 §5 Connection; 05 §17). Its identity is its room and direction. barrier, optional (barrier@1), names the Barrier whose one shared state the exit passes through (21 §5 Barrier; 05 §25 coherent connections): move through it is refused while it is closed (exit_closed) or locked (exit_locked); an exit without one means what it always meant. A reciprocal exit is authored in the destination room (00a §2); faces pair by opposite direction: an exit's reciprocal face is its destination's exit in the opposite compass direction when that exit leads back to its room, and an exit with a barrier needs a reciprocal face naming the same barrier (BARRIER_MISMATCH at each face otherwise). One-way and bent barrier passages (no reciprocal face, or an opposite-direction exit that leads elsewhere) are rejected for now and may be allowed later; an exit without a barrier is BARRIER_MISMATCH only when its reciprocal face names one.

climb.description: Toolbox row 30 (docs/system/mechanics.md rope and climb): crossing this directed exit is a climb. A mover whose body holds item (directly or in a container) climbs down as on any exit; one without it falls: the move still happens and also costs damage HP, never below 1 (a fall never kills), narrated by fell. The cartridge declares an hp pool (RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID otherwise). NPCs never take a climb face.

corpse_ingress.description: Close this directed exit while the named global fact has the specified value, except for the living owner of a nonempty player corpse in its destination. The exception is rechecked at movement admission.

hidden_until.description: Toolbox row 11 (docs/system/mechanics.md hidden passages): for the commanded character this directed exit does not exist (not listed, not seen through, absent from the map, a move through it not_found) until the named fact has the specified value. No barrier on a hidden face (BARRIER_MISMATCH).

locks.description: Toolbox row G7 (mechanics.md Access locks): traverse, the policy the mover must hold to cross this exit, read by movementPlan after the barrier; failing it refuses permission_denied. Read with no target.

Cue.description: A sense cue (toolbox row G6): what a listener smells, hears or feels from its source. sense is sound, smell or heat; text the authored line (the sense in its words, trap 12); range the rooms it carries through exits, 0 (the source's room only) to 2; when, optional, a condition read for the listener (the player for the view, a reaction's actor for an NPC). Owned by sense_cue@1. Its source is the room, detail, item or NPC, lit fuel source, active status or recipe outcome that declares it.

Cues.description: A source's sense cues (Cue; toolbox row G6), in authored order.

DamageKind.description: A damage kind (toolbox row G2): a closed engine vocabulary shared by attack profiles and NPC resistances. A row that needs a new kind adds it here; a kind never shares a name with a Tag.

DeathCredit.description: Finite authored death credit linking one local attackable NPC, its authored room and a player Boolean fact with false default. Compiler and loader enforce references and unique NPC/fact ownership.

DeathSettings.description: Fixed corpse templates, same-body return room and pool restoration; requires death@1 (docs/system/cartridge.md).

narration.description: A player's death lines outside a combat round (loka-3w3q). player_died: the fall line a bleed or status tick death tells after its tick line (default world.combat.narration.player_died; a drowning tells world.water.drowned instead). woke: told once after every player death, combat included, after the penalty line.

penalty.description: What a player's death costs (toolbox row 47). experience: the body loses floor(experience * percent / 100), never below the threshold of its current level, and narration is told once; it needs world.levelling. items: corpse (the default) moves what the body held into the corpse; kept leaves it on the body.

anyOf.description: Globally stable, immutable reference to a content definition (03 §2; 05 §4: no global content-key namespace). cartridge_id, kind and key are lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters; cartridge_version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata.

DerivedStat.description: One stat's attribute bonus (docs/system/mechanics.md derived stats): floor(sum of per_point * (value - pivot) over terms / divisor), rounded toward minus infinity; value is the player's attribute as attributes@1 reads it. Every number is the cartridge's; divisor defaults to 1.

DescriptionVariant.description: Prose selected by a condition (21 §6 DescriptionVariant; 00a §12): description replaces the base description key when the condition holds for the actor over committed state (policy.schema.json VersionedPolicy; the evaluator is pure, 06 §21). A room's or detail's variants are tried in list order and the first whose condition holds is shown; when none holds, the base description is. Variants are derived, never a mutated description (21 §6). Owned by description_variant (a cartridge with one requires it); its condition's ops by their owners.

DialogueCheck.description: A dialogue choice's check (toolbox row 14, docs/system/mechanics.md dialogue skill checks; check@1): an opposed check as a recipe's (action.schema.json ActionRecipe check, kind opposed) made when the choice is chosen, drawing no RNG: it passes when the actor's level of skill, or value of attribute, is at least rating, or, when npc names an NPC instance of this cartridge that declares the attribute, that NPC's value of it; exactly one of rating and npc (else SCHEMA_VIOLATION invalid_value at the check). key names it in its check_passed or check_failed event (a DefinitionRef of kind check, whose subject is the speaker), shared with no recipe's or other choice's check (DUPLICATE_DEFINITION). On a pass the choice applies as unchecked; on a failure the actor reads failure instead, nothing else of the choice applies and the conversation closes. A skill with growth gains one use per check, passed or failed.

DialogueChoice.description: One option of a dialogue (06 §17, §43): label and narration its text keys; sequence, its fact.assign consequences in order (a declared fact of the cartridge at the one scope it allows, a value of its type, as a recipe's: fact@1 emits fact_changed when the value changes); hand_over, the item role the actor's body gives to the npc role (an item_acquired with that NPC as holder, as give); accept, a quest of this cartridge the choice activates as quest@1's activation does (quest.activate at player scope and quest_activated; the choose is invalid_state when accept_quest would be: the actor already has an instance of it, or its offer, if declared, has a policy that fails), never with a hand_over (activation and acquisition in one decision conflict: OUTCOME_MISMATCH). The choose that selects it applies all of them, resolves the dialogue's quest or activates the accepted one, and resolves the choice in one decision; its outcome is the choice_id. API1.7 receive {item, from} transfers the selected bound NPC-held item into the actor body, only while resolving a quest before API1.10; API1.10 also permits nonterminal receive. Receive is never combined with accept/hand_over. API1.7 fact.adjust applies a safe integer amount to a declared bounded integer fact using checked addition then authored bounds, lowered to fact.assign. Optional (toolbox row 14): check (DialogueCheck), an opposed check made when the choice is chosen; a checked choice carries only label, narration, sequence, availability and check, in a dialogue with no quest and no riddle, and its sequence grants no skill (else OUTCOME_MISMATCH at its check).

escort.description: API1.11 escort@1: npc names a bound NPC role. Start/rejoin are nonterminal; complete resolves the dialogue’s same quest.

DialogueRole.description: A dialogue role's participant, as action.schema.json NarrationParticipant's npc or item branch (the actor is implicit): an NPC or item of this cartridge (else UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE).

EscortStatus.description: The bounded escort lifecycle: following moves with the actor, separated waits for explicit rejoin, completed never follows again.

ExecutionProfile.description: A hosting profile a cartridge supports or a deployment uses: the canonical execution-profile vocabulary (07 §3; 09 §20 reuses it).

anyOf.description: true or false.
One of values (order and duplicates carry no meaning); default is one of them, which the compiler checks.
A safe integer within the optional inclusive bounds; the compiler checks default against them.

FactType.description: A fact's value type and default (03 §7). The types chapter one declares (00a §6): bool, enum over Keys, and int with optional inclusive bounds. The value itself is a FactValue (delta.schema.json).

FactValue.description: The value of a fact, in fact.assign, fact_compare and fact_changed: a Key, a safe integer or a boolean, the value types FactSpec declares (fact.schema.json; 03 §7). Which one a fact takes is its FactType, which the compiler checks.

cues.description: Cues active only while this source is lit (toolbox row G6).

FuelSpec.description: Immutable authored source or supply metadata; sources bind one compatible supply and their narration keys.

InspectableDetail.description: A lightweight keyed detail of a room (21 §6 InspectableDetail): the aliases a player can name it by, the first of which also names it when a lookup is ambiguous, and its description text key (05 §18). Not a RuntimeEntity: a fresh world gives it a target id only (numeric profile, Initial world ids). Two details of one room may share an alias (an ambiguous lookup lists both, 04 §18), but the first alias must be the detail's own and in the form a lookup produces (no empty word, not starting with at, the, a or an), or the player could not pick it by name (UNREACHABLE_DETAIL). Its variants (DescriptionVariant) select other prose by condition. Owned by inspectable_detail (a cartridge with details requires it). R5 freezes this v1 shape (14 §R5): perception, reveal facts and contextual actions join as optional fields.

tool.description: Toolbox row 19: Harvest needs a held item whose definition declares tag.

rating.description: Toolbox row G5 (docs/system/mechanics.md opposed checks): the value an opposed recipe check against this detail must reach.

readable.description: Optional readable@1 prose and its place-action label (docs/system/mechanics.md readable@1); both keys resolve in the text catalog.

title.description: Optional page title the Book shows for this detail (loka-x6t.120; docs/system/mechanics.md inspectable_detail@1): it resolves in the text catalog (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE); without it a page falls back to its kind's title or the description.

ItemAffect.description: One attribute modifier an item grants its wearer while worn (docs/system/mechanics.md item slots and affects, toolbox row 3), or an active status grants its holder (StatusDefinition.modifies, row 2c; the shape of an ancestry's attribute modifier): attribute, an attribute of this cartridge; modifier, the signed amount added to the value attributes@1 reads. The number is the cartridge's.

ItemBandage.description: A directly held item opted into exact bleed treatment.

ItemEdible.description: D4 held-food metadata; a complete original item grants capped recovery when Eat commits.

amount.description: Positive integer; the canonical numeric profile supplies the safe-integer upper limit.

applies.description: Toolbox row hs-5: statuses Eat applies to the eater's body after the recovery and any cures, through the shared status apply (status_applied on a first application, immune holds, a refresh is silent); none may modify an hp-maximum attribute.

cures.description: Statuses (toolbox row 1) this food ends when eaten; eating is allowed at the pool maximum while one of them is active.

ItemLocation.description: Where an item starts (00a §12 location): in a room, held by an NPC, or inside another item of the same cartridge, named by the field its kind selects. The containers an artifact's items start in form no cycle (CONTAINMENT_CYCLE) and hold at most their capacity (CAPACITY_EXCEEDED).

ItemReadable.description: API1.24: one explicit held-item Read, with optional declared Boolean topic grant.

KernelApiRange.description: The kernel_api compatibility range a cartridge declares (05 §3 'Compatibility versions'): at_least inclusive, below exclusive, so '>=1.3 <2.0' is at_least 1.3, below 2.0.

KernelApiVersion.description: A kernel_api version, MAJOR.MINOR without leading zeros (05 §3).

Key.description: A stable semantic key: lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters, the DefinitionRef segment rule (03 §2). Used for action keys, directions, choices, outcomes and key-valued facts.

KnockResponse.description: A local barrier face’s authored answer when the named NPC is in the destination room, and its no-answer text.

LiquidRow.description: Exact vessel contents: null iff zero, positive declared kind bounded by immutable capacity.

anyOf.description: Globally stable, immutable reference to a content definition (03 §2; 05 §4: no global content-key namespace). cartridge_id, kind and key are lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters; cartridge_version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata.

LogicalTime.description: Explicit logical time (01 A6; 04 §4). Units are fixed by the authored calendar (calendar@1): time 0 is midnight of day 1, and the hour of day is floor(t / units_per_hour) mod hours_per_day (policy.schema.json time_window).

Loudness.description: How a word was spoken (speech@1; toolbox row G9): whisper reaches the addressee, say the speaker's room, shout the rooms one exit away too.

MapPosition.description: Static integer drawing coordinates for one room; exits remain the sole connection graph.

NameWords.description: Name words (loka-6qi): bare, the text key of the name with no article ("lantern"); optionally article, the article a presenter puts before bare (a, an or the); optionally plural, the text key of the plural ("lanterns"). short stays the phrase narration binds; words exist for presenters that compose a sentence from several names. Each key is in the text catalog.

NarrationParticipant.description: An entity a recipe's narration names, by the field its role selects (like entity.schema.json ItemLocation): an NPC or item of this cartridge, or the command's actor (its body). The compiler reports an npc or item that names no definition of that kind in this cartridge as UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE.

NpcHp.description: Explicit entity-specific HP bounds/start/gain. Requires minimum <= start <= maximum (RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID). Required legacy-shaped birth/save row; no position recovery.

anyOf.description: Every item holds; an empty list is the policy with no condition.
At least one item holds.
The item does not hold.
The resolved target is present to the actor.
The actor holds an item of this definition, directly or inside containers it holds, transitively.
The actor's instance of the quest is in this lifecycle state.

The fact, in the actor's scope, equals this value. An entity or pair fact (toolbox row W2) is read at exactly one subject: npc or item, that definition's authored instance, or subject target, the action's target (false without one); a player or instance fact names none.

with.description: Toolbox row FD4: an npc_pair fact's second NPC, read at the pair (subject toward with).

anyOf.description: 06 §21 time_window, a window of authored calendar hours: floor(time / calendar.units_per_hour) mod calendar.hours_per_day is in `from` inclusive to `to` exclusive, wrapping at day end. The compiler rejects endpoints outside the authored day and equal endpoints (EMPTY_TIME_WINDOW). Owned by schedule@1.
The barrier's current state equals `equals` (room.schema.json BarrierState; closed means closed and unlocked). Owned by barrier@1.
The actor's value of the attribute (cartridge.schema.json AttributeSpec: its start, while nothing writes attributes) is at least at_least. Owned by attributes@1.
Toolbox row 29a: the actor's level (toolbox row 4, derived from its experience; 1 in a cartridge without world.levelling) is at least at_least. Owned by attributes@1.

The current value of the resource on the actor's body (regenerated to now, before the action's costs) is at least at_least; false for an actor without a body. Toolbox row 39: subject subject reads the pool on a reaction's event subject (the actor's body outside a reaction); at_least_percent holds when value * 100 >= percent * the entity's maximum. Exactly one of at_least and at_least_percent. Owned by attributes@1.
API1.11 escort@1: this actor’s typed escort for the named quest instance has this status.

The subject's definition declares the tag (entity.schema.json Tag). Exactly one subject: subject target, the action's target, holding when it is an item whose definition declares the tag (false without a target, for a detail or for an NPC); subject room, the actor's current room; or item, barrier or room, that definition of this cartridge, a constant (tags never change). Owned by tags@1 (toolbox row G1).

The derived sky at the committed clock, never stored (toolbox rows 10 and 31): exactly one of lunar, season or tide (the cut of that calendar cycle containing ((clock - origin) mod period)) or weather (the calendar day's weather table entry) holds when the current phase is that phase; a set of phases is an any of sky leaves. The compiler rejects a phase the named calendar table does not author, or no such table (SCHEMA_VIOLATION). Owned by calendar@1.
The actor's body wears an item whose definition declares tag (toolbox row W25): an item in one of the body's slot holders (equipment@1). False without a body. Owned by equipment@1.

The actor's count of accepted body entries into the room, the current one included, is at least at_least (toolbox row W7): a new character's start room counts once, any other room 0 until entered. Counted only while variety@1 is locked (VisitedRoom.count). Owned by variety@1.

The actor's level in the named skill (skills@1: 1 when acquired, plus each growth threshold its use count has reached; 0 when neither) is at least at_least (toolbox row FD2). Derived on read. Owned by skills@1.

The named population plan has at least at_least living members: slots 1 to cap whose row has a member_id and no replacement_due (toolbox row W12). Derived on read; reads no actor. Owned by population@1.

The subject holds an active status of this definition (status@1 row; toolbox row W6). subject target: the action's target, or, in an entity's own variant (TextVariants), the entity described; false without a target or for a detail. subject self (toolbox row G3 reader 1): the actor's body. subject subject (reader 1): in a reaction's when, the event's subject, the holder a status.apply without item, npc or co_present lands on; false anywhere else. subject room (Built rooms S4, status reader 9): the actor's current room, which is the room being described in a room's or blueprint's variant. Owned by status@1.

An item carrying this property tag (Tag, toolbox row G1) lies directly in the actor's current room: on its floor, not carried and not inside a container there (Homestead hs-6, furnishing). That is the actor's room (the only room the Book describes), as status_active subject room; in a reaction's when the reaction's actor's room. One query step per container row scanned. Owned by containment@1.

The NPC of this definition is present: in the actor's current room and alive (hp above 0 when it has hp); false without a body. Presence, not posture (the player's posture is the position fact). Toolbox row W6. Owned by target_resolution@1.

The NPC of this definition, alive, perceives a cue of sense (toolbox row G6): an active Cue whose source is within its range of the NPC's room, through exits not hidden from the actor, read for the actor (a reaction's actor); in a reaction's condition whose cause is a recipe outcome event (check_failed: failure; check_passed or action_completed: success), only that outcome's cues, from the actor's room. False for an NPC that is dead or nowhere. Owned by sense_cue@1.
Toolbox row FD1: the world clock minus the int fact's value (as fact_compare reads it, at its named NPC or item) is at least at_least; a fact never stamped holds its default. Owned by fact@1.

Policy.description: A pure condition tree (06 §21). all/any/not compose; the leaves are the 06 §21 operators the R6P proof uses (pre-release-proof.md) and the rest are added with their first use, each versioned by its owning capability (VersionedPolicy). fact_compare compares FactValue. stat_compare and resource_compare (attributes@1, 06 §21 amendment 2026-10-03) hold when the actor's attribute value, or the current value of the resource on the actor's body, is at least at_least; below is not, a range is all.

QuestJournal.description: Lifecycle journal texts, selected by quest@1 in GameView (06 §2, §41; 04 §15, c1-journal amendment). All five stage texts are required; outcomes optionally overrides terminal text by outcome key. Outcome keys need not name a dialogue choice. Reveal remains LATER. API1.9 active_variants are checked in order for active quests; the first holding policy supplies text, otherwise ordinary active/objectives_met selection applies. API1.46 hints (toolbox row W23): per stage (active, objectives_met), each after a whole number of real minutes since the stage began (the instance's started_at), strictly ascending, and at least one stage (an empty hints object is a compiler check: the subset has no minProperties); the Journal shows the last one whose time has passed.

QuestObjective.description: A quest's one objective and its evidence policy (06 §3 Objective credit/causation policy, §43; 04 §5.2). current_state: met while policy holds for the actor, evaluated on the state at hand and never stored (the R6P lantern: current possession, so a lantern taken before acceptance counts and one given away no longer does). post_activation_event: met by an item_acquired event whose item is the item `item_acquired` names and whose holder is the actor's body, at a causal position after the instance's activation; the instance then moves to objectives_complete in the same decision, and an acquisition before activation never counts (the Tiny fixture's strict credit; its automatic resolution is not part of this vocabulary yet).

QuestState.description: Persisted QuestInstance lifecycle state (06 §1). Availability is derived, not a state.

RecipeCost.description: One resource cost of an ActionRecipe (21 §7 Cost): the actor's body pays amount of a resource of the cartridge on every admitted perform, failure included (04 §5.0). A perform whose body cannot pay (current value minus amount below the resource's minimum) is rejected insufficient_resource before any RNG draw, and changes nothing.

RecipeCraft.description: What a craft recipe uses up and makes (docs/system/mechanics.md Craft; Homestead hs-10): consume, yield or both. consume: on every accepted perform, failure included, the first quantity of the listed items the actor's body holds directly (lowest EntityId first; one inside a worn or carried container does not count) move to the holder to; while the body holds fewer the perform is rejected invalid_state and the offer is unavailable, its reason's message reason when declared. yield: unless the outcome is failure, one of the listed items directly in the holder from (lowest EntityId first) moves to the body, with item_acquired after the check's events; while from holds none the perform is rejected invalid_state and the offer is unavailable with no message. Every moved item passes the body's carrying limits (give rules). The compiler (lib/loka/content/replenish.ex) refuses a template location, a holder with no placed entity (a spawn-template NPC or template item), an item holder that is not a container, duplicate items, and an unresolved item, holder or reason.

RecipeNarration.description: A recipe outcome's narration (21 §4 NarrationSpec): the actor's line, the observers' line, and the entities the actor's line names, each resolved and pinned when the outcome commits (06 §43; text.schema.json Text participants).

anyOf.description: Assign a fact.
Emit a custom event.
Toolbox row G4: end the recipe target's active status of this definition, as a cure does (status@1); nothing when it is not active.

Toolbox row 29b (spell recipes only, compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION): start or refresh this status on the named NPC's instance, else on an aimed spell's target, else on the caster's body, as a reaction's status.apply does (status@1: a dead NPC or an immune holder takes nothing; a first application emits status_applied while a reaction listens).

Toolbox row 29b (spell recipes only): the named NPC's instance (without npc, an aimed spell's target; an unaimed spell requires npc, compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION), when alive, loses amount hp of this damage kind after its resistances (row G2), stopping at 0; a loss to 0 runs the death sequence with the caster as killer and credited character, and closes the NPC's encounter when it is the only opponent.

Toolbox row 29b (spell recipes only): ignite the named fuel source (without item, an aimed spell's target; an unaimed spell requires item, compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION) as the ignite verb does (light@1), when the caster holds it and the verb would admit it; otherwise nothing.
Adjust a resource of the actor's body by `by`, stopping at its bounds.

Built rooms S6 (detail-target recipes only, at most one per sequence, construction@1): raise blueprint at the recipe target's room (its site) toward direction for the actor, as a build service does (service.schema.json); success outcome only (the compiler refuses it elsewhere, lib/loka/content/construction.ex). Admission refuses the perform while the build would be refused (service.site_taken, service.construction_full).

RecipeStep.description: One registered operation of a recipe outcome's explicit sequence (04 §5.2 step 4, §5.3; 05 §28: never a generic setter or an untyped effect). fact.assign sets a declared fact of the cartridge, at the one scope the fact allows, to a value of its type (the host emits fact_changed at this step's causal position when the value changes, fact@1). event.emit emits the cartridge's custom event of this key (EventPayload custom_event, action_recipe@1), whose subject is the recipe's target. resource.adjust adds by (negative: subtracts) to a resource of the actor's body, chained after the costs and any earlier adjust of it, stopping at the resource's bounds (DikuMUD-style: healing at full health heals nothing); this saturation is the step's declared meaning, not a silent clamp (04 §5.1): the rule computes the stopped value and proposes an exact delta resource.adjust to it, or none when the value does not change. Costs never saturate (RecipeCost).

anyOf.description: Toolbox row 29a (word bar S2): a spell, cast only by the cast command typing its word (no other spell recipe has it), never offered by key or performed; it acts on the caster's body. With aimed (loka-x6t.109) it is cast at one entity in those scopes of the caster's room or body (cast target_id; invalid_target otherwise, after the word's own invalid_state), its policy read with that target, offered on each admitted target's GameView entry and never in spell_words; an unaimed spell refuses a target_id. learned names a bool fact of this cartridge (FACT_TYPE_MISMATCH otherwise; a per_subject fact is FACT_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED, loader only): while it reads false for the caster, a cast of the word is refused exactly as an unknown word and GameView spell_words omits it.

RecipeTarget.description: What an ActionRecipe acts on (06 §20 target; 21 §7 TargetSpec): one inspectable detail, by its room and its key in that room's details, offered only while the actor is in that room; or (toolbox row G4) a use: a tool the actor holds, used on another item on the floor of the actor's room or carried directly, both chosen by the invocation (perform item_id and target_id), the recipe keyed by the tool's properties here and the target's through its policy (has_tag and status_active, subject target), never by item ids; or (toolbox row 29a) a spell named by its word, castable by an actor only while its learned fact reads true for them.

ReleaseVersion.description: A release version (05 §3 version, §12): MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata, at most 64 characters.

ResistancePercent.description: A resistance percent (toolbox row G2): negative is a weakness.

Resistances.description: Toolbox row G2 (docs/system/mechanics.md damage model): an NPC's percent resistance per damage kind (DamageKind) and per material tag (Tag) of the weapon whose own attack strikes (an unarmed or NPC attack has none); negative is a weakness. An attack sums the entries for its kind and each such tag, clamps the sum to -100..100 and scales its damage by (100 - sum) / 100, rounded down. Its members are exactly the DamageKind and Tag values.

ResourceInt.description: A resource bound, value or amount: a 32-bit signed integer, so that every derived value (regeneration, costs, adjustments) stays exact in every kernel's arithmetic.

RestBinding.description: One exact paid Rest binding: authored bed, first-credit fact and sole quest.

SceneStep.description: The installed closed scene step subset; no arbitrary writes.

escrow.description: Toolbox row 20a: the first quantity of these directly held items move to the custody room with the order. Row 20b: ready_after with output (an item lying in custody) adds a work job a claim waits for; cancel returns the inputs, never the fee. Row kgd.70: output with no ready_after is a barter, handed from custody to the body with the inputs, no job.

anyOf.description: Built rooms S2 (construction@1): raise blueprint at site's direction. blueprint is one of site.blueprints and direction one of site.directions (SCHEMA_VIOLATION invalid_value otherwise). Refused service.site_taken while a built room holds that site direction and service.construction_full at world.construction.max_total. Built rooms S3: fact with escrow (ready_after, no output) makes it a commission: the order sets fact true, moves the inputs to custody and schedules an order job; when due the job raises the room for its owner and sets fact false (refunding the inputs when the site is taken or construction full by then). Cancel (a cancel benefit naming this service) returns the inputs, never the fee.

escrow.description: Built rooms S3: the first quantity of these directly held items move to the custody room with the order; ready_after seconds later the order job raises the room.

anyOf.description: Built rooms S4 (construction@1): mend the built room at site's direction. Refused service.nothing_to_mend unless that room's blueprint ruin status is active on it; otherwise the mend cures ruin and applies the blueprint's weathering again. site and direction as build's.

escrow.description: The first quantity of these directly held items move to the custody room with the mend (spent at once).

anyOf.description: Built rooms S5 (construction@1): raze the live built room at site's direction. Refused service.nothing_to_raze without one, permission_denied unless the actor raised it, service.occupied while an entity that cannot move (a corpse) lies in it; otherwise its statuses end, everything on its floor moves to the site and a tombstone (built row) is written. site and direction as build's.

ServiceBenefit.description: Closed paid entitlement, finite meal recovery, provider-owned complete liquid serving (recovery is MV only) or, toolbox row 21, a repair adding up to amount to the wielded weapon's durability fact; or, toolbox row 20b, a claim or cancel of the named commission service's timed escrow order; or, toolbox row 25, a deposit or withdraw of amount between the player's pool and the vault NPC's, mirrored in the account fact, the price being the fee; or, Built rooms S2 to S4, a build or mend of a site's room.

Shop.description: A finite NPC shop: conserved resource, exact authored item offers and committed purchase/sale narration keys (B3).

buy_discount.description: A buy price of floor(buy * numerator / denominator), at least minimum, while its condition holds: exactly one of skill (the actor has the skill usable) or (toolbox row 15) friendly, the shop's NPC disposed friendly to the actor (its disposition).

ShopOffer.description: One exact authored shop item definition with its positive buy and sell prices; custody determines availability (B3).

stock.description: Toolbox row W11: sell from this identity set, items[0] the offer's item, at buy[n-1] while the shopkeeper directly holds n of it; buy has one entry per item and buy[0] equals the offer's buy.

stolen.description: Toolbox row 34: this shopkeeper is a fence; sell takes only an instance whose world.theft stolen fact is true, and a shop without it only one whose fact is false. Never on a stock offer.

SlotKey.description: An equipment slot (equipment@1; 00 §4.4 and 21 §8 as amended by c1-equipment): the thirteen keys. A fresh world makes one holder entity inside the body per slot some item declares, capacity 2 for finger (two fingers, toolbox row 3) and 1 for every other slot (numeric profile, Slot holder ids).

SpokenKeyword.description: An authored spoken keyword (speech@1; toolbox row G9): 1 to 32 lowercase ASCII letters, compared with a case-folded say, whisper or shout word.

Tag.description: A property tag (toolbox row G1): a closed engine vocabulary, so every mechanic that gives a tag meaning and every cartridge that declares one share its spelling. Item, barrier and room definitions declare tags; the has_tag policy leaf (tags@1) reads them. A row whose mechanic needs a new tag adds it here. A room tagged air, chasm or water (status reader 7) admits a move into it only for a body whose active statuses pass that tag. Toolbox row 28 gives cursed no meaning of its own (has_tag, wearing and resistances see it as any tag): content marks a curse-bearing item with it for a wearing leaf in that item's name variant. Toolbox row 43a adds road and marsh, which have no meaning of their own: cartridge.json world.movement.terrain gives a room tag a fare percent. Aimed spells (loka-x6t.109) add lamp, which has no meaning of its own: content marks a light an aimed lux may target.

anyOf.description: The action takes no target.
One entity from the listed scopes.

TargetSpec.description: The candidate scopes an action's target is resolved from (21 §7): the scopes the R6P proof resolves to an EntityId. Inspectable details use target-only EntityIds and the inspectable_details scope. equipped, connections, party and privileged global scope are added with their first use, with a target identity for non-entity targets (21 §6). Accepted kinds and capabilities are added with the capability registry.

TextCatalog.description: The cartridge's default-locale strings (05 §18: stable string ids, inline defaults extracted into a catalog): each TextKey to its display text, 1 to 4,096 characters. One locale only; per-locale catalogs, plural rules and binding placeholders join later under a new cartridge format tag. Every text key a room, detail, variant, item, NPC (short, room_line, description) or action (label, accessibility) uses has an entry; a string marks its tappable words inline as touch links (owner decision 2026-09-25, Q3): the words in square brackets, which link the thing whose text it is, optionally followed at once by a target key in parentheses, which links that detail of the room or item or NPC of the cartridge instead (DiagnosticCode UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE, TOUCH_LINK_MISSING), so each locale marks its own words; a host showing plain text shows the words without the brackets and target; the compiler reports a missing one as UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE.

TextKey.description: A localization string id, never display text (04 §15; 05 §18): lowercase dotted snake_case of at most 128 characters, the ActionDefinition label rule. Text carries its interpolation bindings.

TextVariants.description: Toolbox row W6: variants of one entity text (short, room_line or description), the first whose condition holds replacing it (DescriptionVariant, as for a room's description); the base text stays mandatory. Each condition reads with the entity itself as the target (status_active subject target).

TimePolicy.description: Opt-in M1-A elapsed logical seconds per real second; absence retains legacy play_time. Requires schedule@1. Millisecond conversion and fractional remainder belong to host M1-B. Integer type obeys loka-numeric-v1 safe range.

recap_after_minutes.description: Toolbox row W27, opt-in: an elapsed settlement spanning at least this many real minutes opens the next Book page with one away recap block. At most one week (10080).

UseTool.description: Toolbox row G4: what a use recipe's tool must be, at least one property: an item whose definition declares tag, and a vessel holding some of liquid (quantity above 0).

VersionedPolicy.description: A policy tree with the AST version it was written against (14 §R3A 'core policy AST/versioning'). A new leaf operator is versioned by its owning capability, which the cartridge must lock (capability_registry.json policies); adding an operator to a capability version that is already installed takes that capability's next version. A changed meaning of an existing operator takes a new policy_version.

VesselSpec.description: Opted finite vessel shell with authored positive capacity and initial contents.

WaterSettings.description: D6 exact paired surface/bottom routes, usable skill, entry load/cost, absolute submersion duration and authored warning/death copy; real_elapsed content only.

WeaponProfile.description: An equipped weapon's required skill and authored attack profile.

durability.description: Toolbox row 21: the bounded int entity fact holding this weapon's durability (its default is a new weapon's) and the amount each hit of its own attack takes off; at the fact's minimum it is broken and strikes unarmed.

ranged.description: Toolbox row 17: the weapon shoots in an encounter's round 1, spending one of the body's ammo resource pool; it never strikes in melee.

WeatherEntry.description: One weather of a calendar's weather table (toolbox row 31): each calendar day takes one entry with probability weight / total weight, by a hash of the world id and the day, never the authority RNG. wet: an exposed room's flame will not light (light@1 ignite). Phases are unique in the table.

Word.description: One spoken word (speech@1; toolbox row G9): 1 to 32 ASCII letters, the riddle answer's bound. The rule case-folds it and compares it only with authored keywords; it never reaches narration.

WorldSettings.description: The cartridge's world settings (owner decision world parameters; 00 §4 and 04 §15 as amended 2026-10-02), each optional with an engine default: movement.cost, what a move costs the body (movement@1; default 1 mv when the cartridge declares mv), its resource a pool of this cartridge (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE otherwise); movement.terrain, the percent each destination room tag scales that cost by (row 43a; default none); movement without cost, or with terrain; bands, the condition band table of every pool without its own (resource.schema.json BandTable; default the 04 §15 table). An optional field of loka-cartridge-v2: the tag stays, and the compiler writes it only when the source authors it. In source it is cartridge.json's world, beside entry.

carry.description: Opts into the voluntary Take ceiling (docs/system/mechanics.md containment@1); every item must author mass_grams. No engine default.

construction.description: Built rooms S1 (construction@1): max_total, the most structures built in this world at once.

derived.description: Opts into stats derived from the player's attributes (docs/system/mechanics.md derived stats, toolbox row 2; attributes@1). Each table's bonus is added to the authored number it modifies: hit_chance to the attack profile's chance (clamped 0..100), damage to both damage_min and damage_max (clamped at 0), carry_grams to carry.max_grams (clamped at 0), hp_max to the player body's hp maximum (clamped at the pool minimum). hit_chance and damage need world.combat; carry_grams needs world.carry. An NPC keeps its authored profile unless it declares attributes (toolbox row G3): then hit_chance and damage apply to its attack with its own values.

gear_budget.description: Balance tool 6b (docs/system/cartridge.md item affect declarations; attributes@1): the signed affect total an item in each slot may carry at intended level 1 (per_slot) and what each level above 1 adds (per_level). The engine ignores it at runtime; only the power report reads it.

per_slot.description: Keyed by SlotKey (entity.schema.json), at least one (a compiler check, SCHEMA_VIOLATION too_few_items: the subset has no minProperties); a slot it omits is unbudgeted, never 0.

group.description: Toolbox rows G8, 22a and 22b: member, stay and fight each name a bool pair fact read at each NPC; wage pays every member amount of a conserved resource each `every` clock units (docs/system/cartridge.md#group-declarations).

identity.description: Toolbox rows W15 and FD9 (mechanics.md Recognition and earned titles): the player's displayed name, the text key name, varied by name_variants (TextVariants, first match wins; subject target is the player's body). GameView projects it as actor_name.

levelling.description: Opts into experience and levelling (docs/system/mechanics.md experience and levelling, toolbox row 4; attributes@1). thresholds are the strictly increasing experience totals that reach levels 2, 3 and so on; points_per_level the attribute points each level grants; kills the experience a credited kill of each NPC definition grants; level_up the receipt line when a decision reaches a new level. Every number is the cartridge's.

mount.description: Toolbox row 43b: riding names a bool pair fact, per subject and scoped to player, read at each NPC with a mount declaration; such an NPC carries its rider (docs/system/cartridge.md#mount-declarations).

terrain.description: Terrain movement costs (row 43a; docs/system/mechanics.md, Terrain movement costs): a room tag to the percent a move into a room carrying it scales the fare by, applied after status cost_percent, in the room's authored tag order, rounded down each step. The key pattern repeats the entity.schema.json Tag enum, so a Tag added there is refused here until this list follows (fail closed).

theft.description: Toolbox rows 33 and 34 (mechanics.md Theft, fence and witnessed offense): take may lift an item a living NPC in the actor's room directly holds. The victim notices when the actor's level in skill is below the victim's value of attribute (absent: 0); every other living NPC there that is not blind and the actor's body is not concealed from also sees. Containment alone sets the per_subject instance bool fact stolen true on the item; a seen theft emits custom_event noticed (subject: the thief's body) and says narration.seen, an unseen one narration.unseen.

trails.description: Toolbox row W13 (mechanics.md Tracks and trails): a trail is fresh while now minus its time is below fresh_for (logical seconds); a passed track check appends leads[<exit>], one per direction some room's exit uses.

partial.AttackProfile.description: Cartridge-owned hit chance and positive damage bounds. Compiler and loader enforce damage_min <= damage_max.

crit.description: Toolbox row G2: a hit whose accuracy roll (the hit draw, uniform in [0, 100)) is below chance is critical and its damage is multiplied by multiplier, before resistances.

partial.Connection.description: One directed exit to another room of the same cartridge (21 §5 Connection; 05 §17). Its identity is its room and direction. barrier, optional (barrier@1), names the Barrier whose one shared state the exit passes through (21 §5 Barrier; 05 §25 coherent connections): move through it is refused while it is closed (exit_closed) or locked (exit_locked); an exit without one means what it always meant. A reciprocal exit is authored in the destination room (00a §2); faces pair by opposite direction: an exit's reciprocal face is its destination's exit in the opposite compass direction when that exit leads back to its room, and an exit with a barrier needs a reciprocal face naming the same barrier (BARRIER_MISMATCH at each face otherwise). One-way and bent barrier passages (no reciprocal face, or an opposite-direction exit that leads elsewhere) are rejected for now and may be allowed later; an exit without a barrier is BARRIER_MISMATCH only when its reciprocal face names one.

climb.description: Toolbox row 30 (docs/system/mechanics.md rope and climb): crossing this directed exit is a climb. A mover whose body holds item (directly or in a container) climbs down as on any exit; one without it falls: the move still happens and also costs damage HP, never below 1 (a fall never kills), narrated by fell. The cartridge declares an hp pool (RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID otherwise). NPCs never take a climb face.

corpse_ingress.description: Close this directed exit while the named global fact has the specified value, except for the living owner of a nonempty player corpse in its destination. The exception is rechecked at movement admission.

hidden_until.description: Toolbox row 11 (docs/system/mechanics.md hidden passages): for the commanded character this directed exit does not exist (not listed, not seen through, absent from the map, a move through it not_found) until the named fact has the specified value. No barrier on a hidden face (BARRIER_MISMATCH).

locks.description: Toolbox row G7 (mechanics.md Access locks): traverse, the policy the mover must hold to cross this exit, read by movementPlan after the barrier; failing it refuses permission_denied. Read with no target.

anyOf.description: Globally stable, immutable reference to a content definition (03 §2; 05 §4: no global content-key namespace). cartridge_id, kind and key are lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters; cartridge_version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata.

partial.DialogueCheck.description: A dialogue choice's check (toolbox row 14, docs/system/mechanics.md dialogue skill checks; check@1): an opposed check as a recipe's (action.schema.json ActionRecipe check, kind opposed) made when the choice is chosen, drawing no RNG: it passes when the actor's level of skill, or value of attribute, is at least rating, or, when npc names an NPC instance of this cartridge that declares the attribute, that NPC's value of it; exactly one of rating and npc (else SCHEMA_VIOLATION invalid_value at the check). key names it in its check_passed or check_failed event (a DefinitionRef of kind check, whose subject is the speaker), shared with no recipe's or other choice's check (DUPLICATE_DEFINITION). On a pass the choice applies as unchecked; on a failure the actor reads failure instead, nothing else of the choice applies and the conversation closes. A skill with growth gains one use per check, passed or failed.

partial.DialogueChoice.description: One option of a dialogue (06 §17, §43): label and narration its text keys; sequence, its fact.assign consequences in order (a declared fact of the cartridge at the one scope it allows, a value of its type, as a recipe's: fact@1 emits fact_changed when the value changes); hand_over, the item role the actor's body gives to the npc role (an item_acquired with that NPC as holder, as give); accept, a quest of this cartridge the choice activates as quest@1's activation does (quest.activate at player scope and quest_activated; the choose is invalid_state when accept_quest would be: the actor already has an instance of it, or its offer, if declared, has a policy that fails), never with a hand_over (activation and acquisition in one decision conflict: OUTCOME_MISMATCH). The choose that selects it applies all of them, resolves the dialogue's quest or activates the accepted one, and resolves the choice in one decision; its outcome is the choice_id. API1.7 receive {item, from} transfers the selected bound NPC-held item into the actor body, only while resolving a quest before API1.10; API1.10 also permits nonterminal receive. Receive is never combined with accept/hand_over. API1.7 fact.adjust applies a safe integer amount to a declared bounded integer fact using checked addition then authored bounds, lowered to fact.assign. Optional (toolbox row 14): check (DialogueCheck), an opposed check made when the choice is chosen; a checked choice carries only label, narration, sequence, availability and check, in a dialogue with no quest and no riddle, and its sequence grants no skill (else OUTCOME_MISMATCH at its check).

escort.description: API1.11 escort@1: npc names a bound NPC role. Start/rejoin are nonterminal; complete resolves the dialogue’s same quest.

partial.DialogueRole.description: A dialogue role's participant, as action.schema.json NarrationParticipant's npc or item branch (the actor is implicit): an NPC or item of this cartridge (else UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE).

cues.description: Cues active only while this source is lit (toolbox row G6).

partial.FuelSpec.description: Immutable authored source or supply metadata; sources bind one compatible supply and their narration keys.

partial.InspectableDetail.description: A lightweight keyed detail of a room (21 §6 InspectableDetail): the aliases a player can name it by, the first of which also names it when a lookup is ambiguous, and its description text key (05 §18). Not a RuntimeEntity: a fresh world gives it a target id only (numeric profile, Initial world ids). Two details of one room may share an alias (an ambiguous lookup lists both, 04 §18), but the first alias must be the detail's own and in the form a lookup produces (no empty word, not starting with at, the, a or an), or the player could not pick it by name (UNREACHABLE_DETAIL). Its variants (DescriptionVariant) select other prose by condition. Owned by inspectable_detail (a cartridge with details requires it). R5 freezes this v1 shape (14 §R5): perception, reveal facts and contextual actions join as optional fields.

tool.description: Toolbox row 19: Harvest needs a held item whose definition declares tag.

rating.description: Toolbox row G5 (docs/system/mechanics.md opposed checks): the value an opposed recipe check against this detail must reach.

readable.description: Optional readable@1 prose and its place-action label (docs/system/mechanics.md readable@1); both keys resolve in the text catalog.

title.description: Optional page title the Book shows for this detail (loka-x6t.120; docs/system/mechanics.md inspectable_detail@1): it resolves in the text catalog (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE); without it a page falls back to its kind's title or the description.

partial.ItemBandage.description: A directly held item opted into exact bleed treatment.

partial.ItemEdible.description: D4 held-food metadata; a complete original item grants capped recovery when Eat commits.

amount.description: Positive integer; the canonical numeric profile supplies the safe-integer upper limit.

applies.description: Toolbox row hs-5: statuses Eat applies to the eater's body after the recovery and any cures, through the shared status apply (status_applied on a first application, immune holds, a refresh is silent); none may modify an hp-maximum attribute.

cures.description: Statuses (toolbox row 1) this food ends when eaten; eating is allowed at the pool maximum while one of them is active.

partial.ItemLocation.description: Where an item starts (00a §12 location): in a room, held by an NPC, or inside another item of the same cartridge, named by the field its kind selects. The containers an artifact's items start in form no cycle (CONTAINMENT_CYCLE) and hold at most their capacity (CAPACITY_EXCEEDED).

partial.ItemReadable.description: API1.24: one explicit held-item Read, with optional declared Boolean topic grant.

partial.KnockResponse.description: A local barrier face’s authored answer when the named NPC is in the destination room, and its no-answer text.

partial.LiquidRow.description: Exact vessel contents: null iff zero, positive declared kind bounded by immutable capacity.

anyOf.description: Globally stable, immutable reference to a content definition (03 §2; 05 §4: no global content-key namespace). cartridge_id, kind and key are lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters; cartridge_version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata.

partial.NameWords.description: Name words (loka-6qi): bare, the text key of the name with no article ("lantern"); optionally article, the article a presenter puts before bare (a, an or the); optionally plural, the text key of the plural ("lanterns"). short stays the phrase narration binds; words exist for presenters that compose a sentence from several names. Each key is in the text catalog.

partial.NarrationParticipant.description: An entity a recipe's narration names, by the field its role selects (like entity.schema.json ItemLocation): an NPC or item of this cartridge, or the command's actor (its body). The compiler reports an npc or item that names no definition of that kind in this cartridge as UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE.

partial.NpcHp.description: Explicit entity-specific HP bounds/start/gain. Requires minimum <= start <= maximum (RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID). Required legacy-shaped birth/save row; no position recovery.

anyOf.description: Every item holds; an empty list is the policy with no condition.
At least one item holds.
The item does not hold.
The resolved target is present to the actor.
The actor holds an item of this definition, directly or inside containers it holds, transitively.
The actor's instance of the quest is in this lifecycle state.

The fact, in the actor's scope, equals this value. An entity or pair fact (toolbox row W2) is read at exactly one subject: npc or item, that definition's authored instance, or subject target, the action's target (false without one); a player or instance fact names none.

with.description: Toolbox row FD4: an npc_pair fact's second NPC, read at the pair (subject toward with).

anyOf.description: 06 §21 time_window, a window of authored calendar hours: floor(time / calendar.units_per_hour) mod calendar.hours_per_day is in `from` inclusive to `to` exclusive, wrapping at day end. The compiler rejects endpoints outside the authored day and equal endpoints (EMPTY_TIME_WINDOW). Owned by schedule@1.
The barrier's current state equals `equals` (room.schema.json BarrierState; closed means closed and unlocked). Owned by barrier@1.
The actor's value of the attribute (cartridge.schema.json AttributeSpec: its start, while nothing writes attributes) is at least at_least. Owned by attributes@1.
Toolbox row 29a: the actor's level (toolbox row 4, derived from its experience; 1 in a cartridge without world.levelling) is at least at_least. Owned by attributes@1.

The current value of the resource on the actor's body (regenerated to now, before the action's costs) is at least at_least; false for an actor without a body. Toolbox row 39: subject subject reads the pool on a reaction's event subject (the actor's body outside a reaction); at_least_percent holds when value * 100 >= percent * the entity's maximum. Exactly one of at_least and at_least_percent. Owned by attributes@1.
API1.11 escort@1: this actor’s typed escort for the named quest instance has this status.

The subject's definition declares the tag (entity.schema.json Tag). Exactly one subject: subject target, the action's target, holding when it is an item whose definition declares the tag (false without a target, for a detail or for an NPC); subject room, the actor's current room; or item, barrier or room, that definition of this cartridge, a constant (tags never change). Owned by tags@1 (toolbox row G1).

The derived sky at the committed clock, never stored (toolbox rows 10 and 31): exactly one of lunar, season or tide (the cut of that calendar cycle containing ((clock - origin) mod period)) or weather (the calendar day's weather table entry) holds when the current phase is that phase; a set of phases is an any of sky leaves. The compiler rejects a phase the named calendar table does not author, or no such table (SCHEMA_VIOLATION). Owned by calendar@1.
The actor's body wears an item whose definition declares tag (toolbox row W25): an item in one of the body's slot holders (equipment@1). False without a body. Owned by equipment@1.

The actor's count of accepted body entries into the room, the current one included, is at least at_least (toolbox row W7): a new character's start room counts once, any other room 0 until entered. Counted only while variety@1 is locked (VisitedRoom.count). Owned by variety@1.

The actor's level in the named skill (skills@1: 1 when acquired, plus each growth threshold its use count has reached; 0 when neither) is at least at_least (toolbox row FD2). Derived on read. Owned by skills@1.

The named population plan has at least at_least living members: slots 1 to cap whose row has a member_id and no replacement_due (toolbox row W12). Derived on read; reads no actor. Owned by population@1.

The subject holds an active status of this definition (status@1 row; toolbox row W6). subject target: the action's target, or, in an entity's own variant (TextVariants), the entity described; false without a target or for a detail. subject self (toolbox row G3 reader 1): the actor's body. subject subject (reader 1): in a reaction's when, the event's subject, the holder a status.apply without item, npc or co_present lands on; false anywhere else. subject room (Built rooms S4, status reader 9): the actor's current room, which is the room being described in a room's or blueprint's variant. Owned by status@1.

An item carrying this property tag (Tag, toolbox row G1) lies directly in the actor's current room: on its floor, not carried and not inside a container there (Homestead hs-6, furnishing). That is the actor's room (the only room the Book describes), as status_active subject room; in a reaction's when the reaction's actor's room. One query step per container row scanned. Owned by containment@1.

The NPC of this definition is present: in the actor's current room and alive (hp above 0 when it has hp); false without a body. Presence, not posture (the player's posture is the position fact). Toolbox row W6. Owned by target_resolution@1.

The NPC of this definition, alive, perceives a cue of sense (toolbox row G6): an active Cue whose source is within its range of the NPC's room, through exits not hidden from the actor, read for the actor (a reaction's actor); in a reaction's condition whose cause is a recipe outcome event (check_failed: failure; check_passed or action_completed: success), only that outcome's cues, from the actor's room. False for an NPC that is dead or nowhere. Owned by sense_cue@1.
Toolbox row FD1: the world clock minus the int fact's value (as fact_compare reads it, at its named NPC or item) is at least at_least; a fact never stamped holds its default. Owned by fact@1.

partial.Policy.description: A pure condition tree (06 §21). all/any/not compose; the leaves are the 06 §21 operators the R6P proof uses (pre-release-proof.md) and the rest are added with their first use, each versioned by its owning capability (VersionedPolicy). fact_compare compares FactValue. stat_compare and resource_compare (attributes@1, 06 §21 amendment 2026-10-03) hold when the actor's attribute value, or the current value of the resource on the actor's body, is at least at_least; below is not, a range is all.

partial.QuestJournal.description: Lifecycle journal texts, selected by quest@1 in GameView (06 §2, §41; 04 §15, c1-journal amendment). All five stage texts are required; outcomes optionally overrides terminal text by outcome key. Outcome keys need not name a dialogue choice. Reveal remains LATER. API1.9 active_variants are checked in order for active quests; the first holding policy supplies text, otherwise ordinary active/objectives_met selection applies. API1.46 hints (toolbox row W23): per stage (active, objectives_met), each after a whole number of real minutes since the stage began (the instance's started_at), strictly ascending, and at least one stage (an empty hints object is a compiler check: the subset has no minProperties); the Journal shows the last one whose time has passed.

partial.QuestObjective.description: A quest's one objective and its evidence policy (06 §3 Objective credit/causation policy, §43; 04 §5.2). current_state: met while policy holds for the actor, evaluated on the state at hand and never stored (the R6P lantern: current possession, so a lantern taken before acceptance counts and one given away no longer does). post_activation_event: met by an item_acquired event whose item is the item `item_acquired` names and whose holder is the actor's body, at a causal position after the instance's activation; the instance then moves to objectives_complete in the same decision, and an acquisition before activation never counts (the Tiny fixture's strict credit; its automatic resolution is not part of this vocabulary yet).

partial.RecipeCraft.description: What a craft recipe uses up and makes (docs/system/mechanics.md Craft; Homestead hs-10): consume, yield or both. consume: on every accepted perform, failure included, the first quantity of the listed items the actor's body holds directly (lowest EntityId first; one inside a worn or carried container does not count) move to the holder to; while the body holds fewer the perform is rejected invalid_state and the offer is unavailable, its reason's message reason when declared. yield: unless the outcome is failure, one of the listed items directly in the holder from (lowest EntityId first) moves to the body, with item_acquired after the check's events; while from holds none the perform is rejected invalid_state and the offer is unavailable with no message. Every moved item passes the body's carrying limits (give rules). The compiler (lib/loka/content/replenish.ex) refuses a template location, a holder with no placed entity (a spawn-template NPC or template item), an item holder that is not a container, duplicate items, and an unresolved item, holder or reason.

partial.RecipeNarration.description: A recipe outcome's narration (21 §4 NarrationSpec): the actor's line, the observers' line, and the entities the actor's line names, each resolved and pinned when the outcome commits (06 §43; text.schema.json Text participants).

anyOf.description: Toolbox row 29a (word bar S2): a spell, cast only by the cast command typing its word (no other spell recipe has it), never offered by key or performed; it acts on the caster's body. With aimed (loka-x6t.109) it is cast at one entity in those scopes of the caster's room or body (cast target_id; invalid_target otherwise, after the word's own invalid_state), its policy read with that target, offered on each admitted target's GameView entry and never in spell_words; an unaimed spell refuses a target_id. learned names a bool fact of this cartridge (FACT_TYPE_MISMATCH otherwise; a per_subject fact is FACT_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED, loader only): while it reads false for the caster, a cast of the word is refused exactly as an unknown word and GameView spell_words omits it.

partial.RecipeTarget.description: What an ActionRecipe acts on (06 §20 target; 21 §7 TargetSpec): one inspectable detail, by its room and its key in that room's details, offered only while the actor is in that room; or (toolbox row G4) a use: a tool the actor holds, used on another item on the floor of the actor's room or carried directly, both chosen by the invocation (perform item_id and target_id), the recipe keyed by the tool's properties here and the target's through its policy (has_tag and status_active, subject target), never by item ids; or (toolbox row 29a) a spell named by its word, castable by an actor only while its learned fact reads true for them.

partial.RestBinding.description: One exact paid Rest binding: authored bed, first-credit fact and sole quest.

escrow.description: Toolbox row 20a: the first quantity of these directly held items move to the custody room with the order. Row 20b: ready_after with output (an item lying in custody) adds a work job a claim waits for; cancel returns the inputs, never the fee. Row kgd.70: output with no ready_after is a barter, handed from custody to the body with the inputs, no job.

anyOf.description: Built rooms S2 (construction@1): raise blueprint at site's direction. blueprint is one of site.blueprints and direction one of site.directions (SCHEMA_VIOLATION invalid_value otherwise). Refused service.site_taken while a built room holds that site direction and service.construction_full at world.construction.max_total. Built rooms S3: fact with escrow (ready_after, no output) makes it a commission: the order sets fact true, moves the inputs to custody and schedules an order job; when due the job raises the room for its owner and sets fact false (refunding the inputs when the site is taken or construction full by then). Cancel (a cancel benefit naming this service) returns the inputs, never the fee.

escrow.description: Built rooms S3: the first quantity of these directly held items move to the custody room with the order; ready_after seconds later the order job raises the room.

anyOf.description: Built rooms S4 (construction@1): mend the built room at site's direction. Refused service.nothing_to_mend unless that room's blueprint ruin status is active on it; otherwise the mend cures ruin and applies the blueprint's weathering again. site and direction as build's.

escrow.description: The first quantity of these directly held items move to the custody room with the mend (spent at once).

anyOf.description: Built rooms S5 (construction@1): raze the live built room at site's direction. Refused service.nothing_to_raze without one, permission_denied unless the actor raised it, service.occupied while an entity that cannot move (a corpse) lies in it; otherwise its statuses end, everything on its floor moves to the site and a tombstone (built row) is written. site and direction as build's.

partial.ServiceBenefit.description: Closed paid entitlement, finite meal recovery, provider-owned complete liquid serving (recovery is MV only) or, toolbox row 21, a repair adding up to amount to the wielded weapon's durability fact; or, toolbox row 20b, a claim or cancel of the named commission service's timed escrow order; or, toolbox row 25, a deposit or withdraw of amount between the player's pool and the vault NPC's, mirrored in the account fact, the price being the fee; or, Built rooms S2 to S4, a build or mend of a site's room.

partial.Shop.description: A finite NPC shop: conserved resource, exact authored item offers and committed purchase/sale narration keys (B3).

buy_discount.description: A buy price of floor(buy * numerator / denominator), at least minimum, while its condition holds: exactly one of skill (the actor has the skill usable) or (toolbox row 15) friendly, the shop's NPC disposed friendly to the actor (its disposition).

anyOf.description: The action takes no target.
One entity from the listed scopes.

partial.TargetSpec.description: The candidate scopes an action's target is resolved from (21 §7): the scopes the R6P proof resolves to an EntityId. Inspectable details use target-only EntityIds and the inspectable_details scope. equipped, connections, party and privileged global scope are added with their first use, with a target identity for non-entity targets (21 §6). Accepted kinds and capabilities are added with the capability registry.

partial.TextKey.description: A localization string id, never display text (04 §15; 05 §18): lowercase dotted snake_case of at most 128 characters, the ActionDefinition label rule. Text carries its interpolation bindings.

partial.UseTool.description: Toolbox row G4: what a use recipe's tool must be, at least one property: an item whose definition declares tag, and a vessel holding some of liquid (quantity above 0).

partial.VersionedPolicy.description: A policy tree with the AST version it was written against (14 §R3A 'core policy AST/versioning'). A new leaf operator is versioned by its owning capability, which the cartridge must lock (capability_registry.json policies); adding an operator to a capability version that is already installed takes that capability's next version. A changed meaning of an existing operator takes a new policy_version.

partial.VesselSpec.description: Opted finite vessel shell with authored positive capacity and initial contents.

partial.WeaponProfile.description: An equipped weapon's required skill and authored attack profile.

durability.description: Toolbox row 21: the bounded int entity fact holding this weapon's durability (its default is a new weapon's) and the amount each hit of its own attack takes off; at the fact's minimum it is broken and strikes unarmed.

ranged.description: Toolbox row 17: the weapon shoots in an encounter's round 1, spending one of the body's ammo resource pool; it never strikes in melee.

partial.source.ActionDefinition.description: An advertised affordance (04 §19; 06 §20; 21 §7): stable key, localization label, target spec, the portable Command type it resolves to (checked against the command registry when content compiles), presentation priority, required input parameters, policy and accessibility description. Aliases, costs and cooldown hints arrive with the text parser and cost capabilities.

partial.source.ActionRecipe.description: A cartridge-local action composed only of registered operations (06 §20 Composed actions / ActionRecipe; 21 §7; 05 §28), invoked by the perform command: its stable key (its ActionSet identity), label, the aliases a player types as its verb (the first words of the command), its target, presentation priority, availability policy (evaluated for the actor; while it fails the action is shown unavailable and perform is rejected), and its outcomes. success is one explicit sequence of at most 16 steps, run in order as one logical decision (04 §5.2) and followed by the engine's action_completed event, and the narration its actor reads; observers is the line others in the room would read, kept for the first host with a second viewer. Optional (R5 S6): a check (RecipeCheck; check@1), whose result selects the outcome: success when it passes, failure when it fails; a recipe has a failure outcome exactly when it has a check (OUTCOME_MISMATCH). A failed check is an accepted perform with outcome failure whose RNG draw and time commit like success (04 §5.0); a recipe without a check has outcome performed. failure's sequence may be empty. duration, a whole number of LogicalTime units, advances the clock by that much on every accepted perform, success or failure (21 §7 Cost, time; 04 §5.4: one time.advance after the outcome's steps); events keep the time the perform was admitted at. action_completed follows the outcome's steps when the outcome is performed or success, never failure. Optional (R5 S6b): costs (RecipeCost, resource@1), paid in order by the actor's body on every admitted perform, failure included; one it cannot pay rejects the perform insufficient_resource before any check or draw. cooldown, a whole number of LogicalTime units: a perform by the same actor before the last admitted attempt's time plus cooldown is rejected cooldown; an admitted attempt, failure included, starts it at its admission time (delta cooldown.start), and at exactly that time plus cooldown the recipe is available again. Admission order: target, cooldown, costs, then the check. Optional (toolbox row W23, fact@1): tip, a text the actor reads once, after the outcome's narration, on the first accepted perform (success, failure or performed); that perform also assigns the engine-owned player fact seen_tip_<key> (bool, default false) true, which the compiler adds, so a recipe with a tip has a key of at most 55 characters and no definition writes that fact (RESERVED_FACT). Optional (loka-j64e): reason, a text key the GameView adds as the message of an offered ActionSet action's (or learned spell word's) unavailable reason while its policy fails (a use-target recipe is hidden then, so its reason is not shown); the perform or cast refusal stays invalid_state. Optional (Homestead hs-10): craft (RecipeCraft), the items a station recipe uses up and makes; a spell recipe has none (SCHEMA_VIOLATION). Result bands join later.

anyOf.description: A luck roll (RecipeCheck).

A deterministic threshold (21 §7 Check: deterministic threshold, difficulty; R5 S6b), owned by check@1 like a luck roll: passes when the actor's body's current value of a resource of the cartridge, read at admission before the recipe's costs, is at least difficulty. It draws no RNG and emits check_passed or check_failed under key; the key rules of RecipeCheck apply.

An opposed check (toolbox rows 5 and G5, docs/system/mechanics.md): passes when the actor's level of skill, or value of attribute, at admission is at least the target detail's rating, or, when npc names an NPC of this cartridge (attribute only, toolbox row G3), that NPC's value of the attribute; draws no RNG. A skill with growth gains one use per perform.
