A track check (toolbox row W13, docs/system/mechanics.md Tracks and trails): passes when the trail of population plan plan (its key; the plan declares trail) in the actor's room is fresh (world.trails.fresh_for); draws no RNG; on success the outcome's lines are followed by world.trails.leads[<exit>].

cues.description: Transient cues of this outcome (toolbox row G6), from the actor's room: perceived only by a cue_perceived condition of a reaction this outcome's check_passed, check_failed or action_completed causes; never stored or shown.

Transient cues of this outcome (toolbox row G6), from the actor's room: perceived only by a cue_perceived condition of a reaction this outcome's check_passed, check_failed or action_completed causes; never stored or shown.

partial.source.BarrierDefinition.description: Shared mutable state for one logical door or gate (21 §5 Barrier), owned by barrier@1 (a cartridge with one requires it), keyed in CompiledCartridge.barriers by DefinitionRefString of kind barrier and named by the exits that pass through it (Connection.barrier): its key; keywords, the Alias words a player names it by after open, close, lock or unlock (the direction of its exit names it too); short, the text key of its short description ("the oak door"); initial, its state in a fresh world (BarrierState); and optionally key_item, the item whose holder may lock and unlock it (has_item: held directly or inside containers the holder holds). Without key_item no one can lock or unlock it. Damaged/repaired and blocked states join as optional fields. Optional tags are its property tags (entity.schema.json Tag, toolbox row G1).

opens_when.description: A condition its open command needs (toolbox row 10, barrier@1): while it fails, open is refused invalid_state; close, lock and unlock and an already open barrier are unaffected.

tags.description: Its property tags (Tag; toolbox row G1), read by the has_tag policy leaf (tags@1).

partial.source.BleedDefinition.description: An authored body bleed duration, tick cadence and HP loss.

partial.source.BlueprintDefinition.description: Built rooms S1 (construction@1; cartridge.md Blueprint and site declarations): one structure a player may build at a room's site (RoomDefinition.site). Its key; title and description, the text keys of the room it becomes; optional variants (DescriptionVariant) and tags (Tag) as a room's; optional locks.enter, the policy the mover must hold to come into the built room, as a room's (toolbox row G7). Nothing builds in S1: the cartridge declares and both compilers check. Built rooms S3: optional max_per_owner, the most rooms of this blueprint one character may own at once; an order at the cap is refused service.construction_full. Built rooms S4: optional weathering, a status of this cartridge the room gets when it is raised (and again when mended); optional ruin, the status a mend cures (a reaction applies it, typically on weathering's status_expired), the mend benefit refuses service.nothing_to_mend unless ruin is active on the room.

partial.source.DialogueDefinition.description: One dialogue node (06 §17; Early R7/R8 D1), keyed in CompiledCartridge.dialogues by DefinitionRefString of kind dialogue, owned by dialogue@1 (a cartridge with one requires it): its key, also the stable action key of its talk (no action's, recipe's, quest's or registered command's: DUPLICATE_DEFINITION) and the beat of the choice it opens; npc, the speaker, whose talk the actor's ActionSet offers while the speaker is in the actor's room, and which is one of the npc roles (a speaker may have several dialogues: a talk to it opens the first, in key order, whose policy holds, and is invalid_state when none does); policy, the talk's availability, rechecked at Choose; prompt, the text key of the pending choice's prompt; roles, the participants talk binds to EntityIds in the durable choice (06 §33, §43: bound once, never re-resolved by name), each an npc that must be in the actor's room or an item the actor's body must hold when a choice is made (else not_present or not_owned), never named actor (the actor is always a participant: DUPLICATE_DEFINITION); quest, the quest a choice resolves through quest@1's resolution, with the choice_id as its outcome (absent in a dialogue with an accept choice, so accepting never resolves: OUTCOME_MISMATCH); and choices, at least one (a compiler check: the subset has no minProperties), each with its label, its narration line (committed with the actor's body and every role pinned), its fact.assign consequences and an optional hand_over of an item role to an npc role. Choices list in key order. API1.9 optionally adds riddle: its existing choice_id, lowercase canonical answer, ordered uppercase letter bank containing every answer letter with multiplicity, and wrong-answer narration text key.

keyword.description: Toolbox row G9 (speech@1): a say or whisper of this word to the speaker opens this dialogue, which talk never offers or opens; no riddle.

label.description: A distinct named Talk label opts that authored control into exact dialogue selection; omission retains first-eligible Talk.

partial.source.ItemDefinition.description: A portable thing (21 §8): its key; keywords, the Alias words a player names it by (target resolution); short, the text key of its short description ("a brass lantern"); room_line, the text key of the line a room shows while it lies there ("A brass lantern sits here."), with room_line_variants (DescriptionVariant, first match wins, as for a room's description); description, the text key examine shows; location, where a fresh world puts it; and optionally container: true, making it a receptacle; only receptacles may declare capacity, the most items held directly (without capacity a receptacle has no limit); optionally slot, the SlotKey it is worn in (equipment@1), with optional affects (ItemAffect), each added to the wearer's attribute while the item is worn (toolbox row 3; needs slot and attributes@1); and optionally barrier, the barrier on it (a container's lid, barrier@1, c1-locks): a barrier of this cartridge that no exit and no other item names (BARRIER_MISMATCH), whose state the door verbs change with the item as target_id; while it is closed or locked, what the item holds is out of reach (containment@1 custody). Optional mass_grams is the shell mass, required for every item when world.carry is authored. Optional tags are its property tags (Tag, toolbox row G1). Optional short_variants and description_variants vary its short and description (TextVariants, toolbox row W6). Optional words are its name words (NameWords, loka-6qi).

container.description: Only explicitly authored receptacles hold items. Absence is false; capacity and barrier require this field.

equip.description: Authored wear and remove words (toolbox row 6a, loka-x6t.20): the Wear and Remove labels and the worn and removed lines. Only with slot; each key is in the text catalog.

give_allowed.description: API1.10: false prevents ordinary Give of this item or any container holding it transitively; absence permits Give when contents allow it. Dialogue hand_over remains legal.

identified.description: Toolbox row 27: a boolean fact, not per_subject; the item is identified while it reads true for the player, and GameView worn sums identified items only (needs affects).

immune.description: Toolbox row G3: statuses that status.apply skips on this item's instance; each names a declared status.

intended_level.description: Balance tool 6b: the level the item is meant for, read only by the power report's gear budget (needs affects; the engine ignores it at runtime).

locks.description: Toolbox row G7 (mechanics.md Access locks): at least one of get, the policy an actor must hold to take this item or anything inside it, and put, the policy to put an item into it (a container only: compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION invalid_value at locks.put). Each is read with this item as target; failing it refuses permission_denied.

mass_grams.description: The item shell mass in grams, excluding its contents. Required on every item under world.carry; explicit zero is valid (docs/system/cartridge.md Carrying settings and item mass).

tags.description: Its property tags (Tag; toolbox row G1), read by the has_tag policy leaf (tags@1).

partial.source.LiquidDefinition.description: Cartridge-owned mass, integer serving and unit labels for a declared liquid.

cures.description: Statuses (toolbox rows 1 and G13) a Drink of this liquid ends; a service serving does not.

partial.source.NpcDefinition.description: A non-player character (00a §4), as a holder of items so far: its key, keywords, short, room_line and description as for an item, the room a fresh world puts it in, and optionally capacity, the most items it holds. Optionally daily_schedule, its daily location schedule (schedule@1), and schedule_cases, its conditional hours (toolbox row W10); dialogue joins with its capability as an optional field. Optional hp opts into entity-specific HP (docs/system/cartridge.md NPC HP overrides). Optional short_variants, room_line_variants and description_variants vary its texts (TextVariants, toolbox row W6). Optional words are its name words (NameWords, loka-6qi).

ask.description: Toolbox row FD7 (speech@1 with topics@1): what the NPC says when asked about a topic. The first answer in authored order whose topic is the one asked and whose when holds (the player as the actor, the NPC as the target) is narrated and grants its grants topic; none: unknown.

attributes.description: Toolbox row G3: this NPC's base attribute values (attributes@1), read at use by an opposed check naming the NPC and by its derived attack; each names a distinct attribute of this cartridge. An attribute it does not list reads its definition start.

walks.description: Toolbox row W26 (mechanics.md NPCs use doors): the step moves only when a path to room exists through exits a walking NPC may cross (breadth first, direction-key order, one query step per exit); the NPC moves in one step, each locked door on the path it holds the key of is unlocked, opened, closed and locked again; no path leaves it where it is.

anyOf.description: Globally stable, immutable reference to a content definition (03 §2; 05 §4: no global content-key namespace). cartridge_id, kind and key are lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters; cartridge_version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata.

walks.description: Toolbox row W26 (mechanics.md NPCs use doors): the step moves only when a path to room exists through exits a walking NPC may cross (breadth first, direction-key order, one query step per exit); the NPC moves in one step, each locked door on the path it holds the key of is unlocked, opened, closed and locked again; no path leaves it where it is.

daily_schedule.description: schedule@1 (06 §13 Behavior/schedule profiles; 21 §10; capability_registry.json definitions): a daily location schedule. Each key is a nonnegative hour of the authored calendar day without a leading zero; the compiler checks it is below hours_per_day. From that hour until the next listed one (wrapping at day end) the NPC belongs in that room of this cartridge. A fresh world schedules one durable job at the first listed hour strictly after its start time; each job's run_job moves the NPC there, if it is elsewhere, and schedules the next (04 §5.4). Until its first job runs, the NPC stays in its room. An empty schedule schedules nothing.

disposition.description: Toolbox row G11: how the NPC stands toward the player, derived when read, never stored: hostile while hostile holds, else friendly while friendly holds, else wary (an NPC without it is wary). Each condition is read with the player as the actor and the NPC as the target, so subject target facts are its pair facts with the player. Hostile refuses talk and trade and, with an attack, engages a player who walks in, saying engage; friendly takes a friendly buy_discount. Toolbox row 35: with arrest instead of engage, a hostile NPC stops a player who walks in and the body goes to arrest.to, saying arrest.narration; no encounter opens.

refuse.description: Book hostile refusal: the line the Book shows on the NPC's page while it is hostile, naming the mood, never the cause; projected as its EntityView refusal.

drops.description: Toolbox row 8 loot table (docs/system/mechanics.md loot tables, world.death): in order, an item this NPC holds at genesis and its percent chance of passing to the corpse when combat kills the NPC; a failed item stays with the dead NPC.

immune.description: Toolbox row G3: statuses that status.apply skips on this NPC's instance; each names a declared status.

locks.description: Toolbox row 33 (mechanics.md Theft, fence and witnessed offense): get, the policy an actor must hold to take an item this NPC directly holds (target: that item); refuses permission_denied.

mount.description: Toolbox row 43b (needs world.mount): this NPC can be ridden. While world.mount.riding is true for (this NPC, a character) and both share a room, the character's moves need a destination room carrying one of terrain, each move's fare is scaled by cost_percent (default 100, floored, applied last) and this NPC moves with the body. Never on a spawn template.

partial.source.PopulationBundle.description: One NPC, directly held item and public NPC corpse template for a bounded population.

partial.source.PopulationPlan.description: One fixed-slot, two-room bounded population with an owned wander and replacement job.

birth_when.description: Toolbox row W12: while false at an occurrence, the plan births nothing above floor. Its tree may use only all, any, not, population_count, time_window, sky and barrier_state (SCHEMA_VIOLATION otherwise, from the compiler).

chance.description: Makes the plan an encounter plan (docs/system/mechanics.md Random encounters, toolbox row 9): each wander-boundary occurrence with an eligible slot draws one uniform(100) and a roll below chance births the first eligible slot. Absent: an RNG-free ecology plan.

floor.description: Toolbox row W12: slots 1 to floor refill at the plan's next occurrence: a member dying there is due at its death time, not after replacement_delay, and they birth whatever birth_when says. At most day_target; refused with chance (SCHEMA_VIOLATION, from the compiler).

hunts.description: Toolbox row W13: a member in a room holding a character's body holds; else each wander step takes the exit of the characters' fresh trail in the member's room when npcPassage admits it, else wanders as before; characters then leave trails (trail_exit, trail_at, instance scope); needs world.trails.

trail.description: Toolbox row W13 (mechanics.md Tracks and trails): a member's wander step and C4 flight write the room left's trail_<key>_exit and trail_<key>_at (engine facts, per room); needs world.trails.

walks.description: Toolbox row W26 (mechanics.md NPCs use doors): the wander step crosses its exit as a walking NPC does (npcPassage with walks): a closed door passes and stays closed, a locked one only for a member holding its key_item (unlocked, opened, closed and locked again); any traverse lock on the exit or enter lock on the room refuses it.

wander_when.description: Toolbox row W12: while false at a wander boundary, no member wanders. The same leaf limit as birth_when.

partial.source.QuestDefinition.description: A quest with one objective (06 §2; R6P pre-release-proof.md), keyed in CompiledCartridge.quests by DefinitionRefString of kind quest, owned by quest@1 (a cartridge with one requires it): its key, also the stable action key of its offer (no action's, recipe's or registered command's: DUPLICATE_DEFINITION); title, the text key of its journal entry (QuestView.title); offer, optional, the accept action its actor's ActionSet lists while the actor has no instance of the quest (label its text key, policy its availability: while it fails the offer is shown unavailable and accept_quest is rejected), which resolves to accept_quest; without one, only a dialogue choice's accept (dialogue.schema.json DialogueChoice) activates the quest; and objective (QuestObjective). Resolution is another capability's: a choice resolves it through quest@1's resolution, which re-checks the objective. Giver, turn-in, prerequisites beyond the offer's policy, further objectives, outcomes and automatic or discovered activation join as optional fields. Optional journal declares lifecycle texts (QuestJournal); selection is computed in QuestView without changing persisted state.

deadline.description: A quest deadline, one object (validate.ts oneOf needs a const discriminator). Legacy (S2): at, fact, trust_fact and trust_amount, no after. Generic (toolbox row W24): exactly one of after (logical units from activation) or at (absolute logical time), no legacy field; activation schedules one engine job and expiry fails the instance with outcome and emits quest_failed. The compiler (lib/loka/content/quests.ex) refuses any other shape (SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

partial.source.ReactionRule.description: Typed reaction owned by reaction@1. Every registered event kind can trigger; each optional filter must equal its payload field (W1). Every delivery runs for the command actor; quest resolution verifies the source instance; a status.apply hits the event's subject or its named item (docs/system/mechanics.md reaction@1). Apply may assign facts (an entity or pair fact, toolbox row W2, at its named npc's or item's instance, else at the event's subject when that is an NPC, item or detail; no subject, no write) or activate a quest on quest_resolved. API1.12 adds typed quest.resolve and quest.fail on fact_changed. Deliveries use one writer group and the existing FIFO budgets; faults commit nothing.

after.description: Toolbox row FD1: the steps run this many logical seconds after delivery, as a reaction job for the delivery's actor, when `when` holds at both times; due no earlier than 1 s after the proposal's clock.

with.description: Toolbox row FD4: an npc_pair fact's second NPC; the step writes at the pair (its subject toward this NPC).

anyOf.description: Toolbox row 15: adds amount to a bounded int fact, clamped to its minimum and maximum, at the subject a fact.assign step writes at.

with.description: Toolbox row FD4: an npc_pair fact's second NPC; the step writes at the pair (its subject toward this NPC).

anyOf.description: Suppress one authored population plan for duration logical seconds from this accepted fact-change cause, preserving current members and closing its current encounter.

Apply one authored status (toolbox row 1) at the cause's time to the event's subject (a body, NPC or thing, row G3), or to the named item's or (row 42, never with item; not a spawn template) NPC's authored instance, or (row W21, co_present) to every living NPC in the event's room; an active one is refreshed; an NPC or item that declares the status immune takes nothing.

co_present.description: Toolbox row W21: the status lands on every living NPC in the event's room (its room_id, else the room directly holding the subject; none for a carried or unplaced one), in EntityId order, never on the player's body; an NPC declaring the status immune takes nothing. Never with item or npc (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

room.description: Status reader 9: the status lands on this room of the cartridge, which holds it as any holder does (its tick changes nothing). Never with item, npc or co_present (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

tag.description: Toolbox row W22 (only with co_present): the status lands instead on every item lying directly in the event's room whose definition carries this tag, the event's subject included, in EntityId order; an item declaring the status immune takes nothing.

anyOf.description: Toolbox row W22 (Beads loka-kgd.96, barrier@1): move barrier, or every barrier on an exit of the event's room (its room_id, else the room directly holding the subject) whose definition carries tag, in direction-key order, to state to, from any state and with no key, opens_when or reach check (a burnt or broken door); each legal step on the way (locked, closed, open) is one barrier.transition and one barrier_changed, and a barrier already at to takes nothing. to locked needs the barrier's key_item, every tagged barrier's for tag (compiler BARRIER_UNREACHABLE_KEY at to).

Toolbox row G3 reader 3: end this status when active on the event's subject (the holder a status.apply without item, npc or co_present lands on), as a cure does: no event, no line. Once per holder and status in a rule, shared with status.apply: the first of the two steps on a pair wins.
Add amount experience to the acting character's levelling row (toolbox row 4), saturating at the ResourceInt maximum; needs world.levelling.

Toolbox row 41 (decay): when the event's subject is an item not already directly in room and not consumed, transfer it from its current holder to room (one entity.transfer, no event, no line, no capacity or reach check); any other subject takes nothing.

Toolbox row FD5 (loka-kgd.22): jumps the named NPC (else the event's subject when it is an NPC) to room, else the event's room, as a schedule move does (no exit, passage or lock), and emits entity_entered_room at the cause's time. Nothing when the NPC is dead, engaged, a following escort, blocked from moving or already there, no room resolves, or the delivery's character is in a running scene. Settle S4-1: plan (never with npc; room required) moves every living member of that population plan instead, in EntityId order, each as above.

Toolbox row 37a (phased world events): births one bundle of the population plan into its home, in the highest free slot up to cap, as the plan job's birth does; no free slot births nothing. No RNG draw (the plan's chance and targets govern its own job only).

Homestead hs-1: one run of the replenish entry key's move, as its job's run does (up to count of its items directly in from, lowest EntityId first, until to holds cap or is full), at once: no job completed or scheduled, no event, no line; nothing when nothing fits. Refused on a rule with after.

Settle S3-1: appends the authored line text to the delivery's narration, after the lines of the steps before it; no op, no event, no actor or subject read. Allowed with after: a fired rule's line joins its job's lines at the due time.
Toolbox row FD1: writes the delivery's logical time into an int fact (no maximum, minimum absent or at most 0) at the subject a fact.assign step writes at, as a fact.assign.

silent.description: Author-time only (mix loka.lint, pass-1 row 3): the rule writes state without a narrate step on purpose. The compiler drops it, so a compiled cartridge never carries it.

partial.source.ReplenishPlan.description: One replenish entry (docs/system/cartridge.md Replenish declarations): each due job moves up to count of items, lowest EntityId first, from the holder from to the holder to until to holds cap of them, then schedules the next at its due time plus every. A move never exceeds to's declared capacity. The compiler (lib/loka/content/replenish.ex) refuses a template location, a holder with no placed entity (a spawn-template NPC or template item), an item holder that is not a container, an item to when any listed item is a container, from equal to to, duplicate items and an unresolved item or holder.

partial.source.RoomDefinition.description: A navigable place (21 §5 Place/Room): its key, its title and description text keys (05 §18; resolved in the cartridge text catalog), and its exits by compass direction, the six-way compass of 00 §4.10 (a direction without an exit is absent), optionally its inspectable details by key, at most 64, its description variants (DescriptionVariant) and its contributions to the ActionSet of an actor in it, applied in order (action.schema.json ActionContribution; R5 S5, optional). Custom named connections (05 §17) join later as a separate optional field. Optional tags are its property tags (entity.schema.json Tag, toolbox row G1).

dark.description: The room is dark (light@1): a player without light, or blind, reads the engine line place.dark instead of the description and sees none of the room's entities. An authored dark_description wins over the engine line.

locks.description: Toolbox row G7 (mechanics.md Access locks): enter, the policy the mover must hold to come into this room, read by movementPlan after the exit's traverse lock; failing it refuses permission_denied. Read with no target.

site.description: Built rooms S1 (construction@1; cartridge.md Blueprint and site declarations): where a structure may be built from this room. directions, the compass directions a built room may open on, none an authored exit of this room (SITE_EXIT_CONFLICT); blueprints, the BlueprintDefinitions that may be built here (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE otherwise).

tags.description: Its property tags (Tag; toolbox row G1), read by the has_tag policy leaf (tags@1) and the terrain fare (row 43a); unique, since a repeated tag would apply its fare percent twice.

on.description: What starts the scene: a story point reached, a quest outcome, or an action recipe's success; an action start names the recipe's room and detail.

partial.source.SceneDefinition.description: Modal narration or the consumed paid-Rest anchored, resumable presentation-only dream.

partial.source.ServiceDefinition.description: Exact original-provider action and conserved quote with one typed immediate benefit.

price.description: Row kgd.70: 0 only on an entitlement with escrow, a barter.

partial.source.SkillDefinition.description: An acquired skill with authored display text and a policy for current qualification.

growth.description: Toolbox row 5 (docs/system/mechanics.md skill growth): strictly increasing use counts reaching levels 2, 3 and so on above the base; the count is the reserved player fact uses_<key>.

hidden.description: Homestead hs-14 (docs/system/mechanics.md Skill trees): the skill is left out of GameView skills, and of NPC lessons, while its prerequisite fails and it is not acquired. A dialogue choice that teaches it is not offered while it is so left out. A non-hidden skill whose prerequisite or qualification reads a hidden skill, a dialogue policy that reads one, and a dialogue label on a dialogue that teaches one are refused.

prerequisite.description: Homestead hs-11 (docs/system/mechanics.md Skill trees): read for the acquiring actor with no target; skill.acquire is refused while it fails. A skill_compare naming this skill is refused.

profession.description: Homestead hs-14 (docs/system/book-ui.md Skill tree details): the profession heading this skill is listed under on the Character page.

partial.source.StatusDefinition.description: Toolbox row 1: one authored timed status on a body. Every tick_every seconds until duration ends, per_tick (signed) is added to resource, saturating at the pool bounds; a negative hp result at zero runs the death sequence. Applied by a reaction status.apply; ended by expiry, an edible that cures it, or death. A reapplication while active refreshes ends_at and keeps the pending tick. Optional modifies (row 2c) adds attribute modifiers, read at use while active; a status with modifies may omit per_tick, and then never ticks (its one job is the expiry).

allows.description: Status reader 4: the only Command types the holding body may issue while the status is active (a modal answer aside); named as blocks; may stand in for per_tick.

blocks.description: Status reader 4: Command types (CommandPayload type) the holding body may not issue while the status is active; each names a registered command other than run_job and elapsed (compiler UNKNOWN_COMMAND); may stand in for per_tick.

concealment.description: Status reader 8: while active on an NPC, the player does not see it; on the player's body, an NPC does not engage it on entry. invisible yields to a see_invisible perception; hidden to none, unless pierced_by. May stand in for per_tick.

cues.description: Cues active while this status is active on a holder, from the holder's room (toolbox row G6).

duration.description: Logical seconds, or permanent (toolbox row W8): no expiry and no job, kept by the same-body return, ended only by a cure; a permanent status never ticks, so it declares no per_tick (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

fear.description: Toolbox row W21: while active on a pack member, its C4 flight is attempted on its every opponent turn, whatever its hp; may stand in for per_tick.

kind.description: Toolbox row loka-x6t.64: the status icon's polarity, shown as GameView ConditionView.kind; wins over the polarity derived from the effect fields.

modifies.description: Toolbox row 2c: while the status is active on a holder, each modifier is added to the holder's attribute as attributes@1 reads it.

movement.description: Status reader 7: the holding body's move cost and the terrain it may cross while the status is active; may stand in for per_tick.

cost_percent.description: Percent of each move's fare (world.movement.cost or 1 mv, after the flee multiplier) the holding body pays, rounded down; several statuses apply in turn in definition order.

passes.description: Terrain tags the holding body may enter: a move into a room tagged air, chasm or water is refused invalid_state unless the body's active statuses pass each such tag.

observed.description: Row G3 (loka-kgd.176): told when a first application lands on an NPC or item in the player's room that the player perceives, or on the room the player stands in (loka-x6t.37); with none, such a holder is silent.

skipped.description: Told, whole, when this status bars its holder's combat blow (loka-x6t.30); with none, the round tells the engine line combat.skipped, its bindings.status this status's label.

per_tick.description: Signed; never 0, required unless modifies, fear, blocks, allows, resistances, perception, concealment or movement is present or duration is permanent, and absent when duration is permanent (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

perception.description: Status reader 6: what the holding body perceives while the status is active. sight blind: every room is dark to it, a lit source or dark sight notwithstanding; dark_sight: sees in an unlit room as an ancestry's dark_sight does; see_invisible: sees a holder of an invisible status. hearing deaf: no sound cue reaches it. At least one field (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION); may stand in for per_tick.

pierced_by.description: Toolbox row 16, only beside concealment: a seer whose attribute value (an NPC's declared value, a player's attributes@1 value) is greater than the holder's skill level sees through the concealment; a holder without a character is never pierced. No draw. While the holder is a player's body, an NPC that engages it on entry ends every active concealment status on it.

resistances.description: Status reader 5: while active on the struck body (the player's or an NPC's), each entry joins the G2 resistance sum of an attack on it, before the one -100..100 clamp; may stand in for per_tick.

partial.source.StoryPointDefinition.description: A story point the cartridge declares (23 §3; 03 §26; Early R7/R8 D2), keyed in CompiledCartridge.story_points by DefinitionRefString of kind story_point, its event story_point_reached owned by dialogue@1: its key, the report's story point (account.schema.json StoryPointReport), and outcomes, at least one (a compiler check: the subset has no minProperties), each reached by its rule-owned trigger: the choice of a dialogue (choose emits story_point_reached after choice_resolved in that decision's root sequence). A trigger site feeds one outcome of one story point (DUPLICATE_DEFINITION), and its dialogue resolves a quest (OUTCOME_MISMATCH otherwise), so a choice reaches it once. In source it is story_points/<key>.json, its dialogue a short reference.

partial.source.TopicDefinition.description: A declared localized topic mapped to its player Boolean knowledge fact.

partial.source.TransportDefinition.description: Paired original boarding detail, destination, conserved fare recipient and corpse recovery rooms.

partial.source.VersionedPolicy.description: A policy tree with the AST version it was written against (14 §R3A 'core policy AST/versioning'). A new leaf operator is versioned by its owning capability, which the cartridge must lock (capability_registry.json policies); adding an operator to a capability version that is already installed takes that capability's next version. A changed meaning of an existing operator takes a new policy_version.

source.ActionDefinition.description: An advertised affordance (04 §19; 06 §20; 21 §7): stable key, localization label, target spec, the portable Command type it resolves to (checked against the command registry when content compiles), presentation priority, required input parameters, policy and accessibility description. Aliases, costs and cooldown hints arrive with the text parser and cost capabilities.

source.ActionRecipe.description: A cartridge-local action composed only of registered operations (06 §20 Composed actions / ActionRecipe; 21 §7; 05 §28), invoked by the perform command: its stable key (its ActionSet identity), label, the aliases a player types as its verb (the first words of the command), its target, presentation priority, availability policy (evaluated for the actor; while it fails the action is shown unavailable and perform is rejected), and its outcomes. success is one explicit sequence of at most 16 steps, run in order as one logical decision (04 §5.2) and followed by the engine's action_completed event, and the narration its actor reads; observers is the line others in the room would read, kept for the first host with a second viewer. Optional (R5 S6): a check (RecipeCheck; check@1), whose result selects the outcome: success when it passes, failure when it fails; a recipe has a failure outcome exactly when it has a check (OUTCOME_MISMATCH). A failed check is an accepted perform with outcome failure whose RNG draw and time commit like success (04 §5.0); a recipe without a check has outcome performed. failure's sequence may be empty. duration, a whole number of LogicalTime units, advances the clock by that much on every accepted perform, success or failure (21 §7 Cost, time; 04 §5.4: one time.advance after the outcome's steps); events keep the time the perform was admitted at. action_completed follows the outcome's steps when the outcome is performed or success, never failure. Optional (R5 S6b): costs (RecipeCost, resource@1), paid in order by the actor's body on every admitted perform, failure included; one it cannot pay rejects the perform insufficient_resource before any check or draw. cooldown, a whole number of LogicalTime units: a perform by the same actor before the last admitted attempt's time plus cooldown is rejected cooldown; an admitted attempt, failure included, starts it at its admission time (delta cooldown.start), and at exactly that time plus cooldown the recipe is available again. Admission order: target, cooldown, costs, then the check. Optional (toolbox row W23, fact@1): tip, a text the actor reads once, after the outcome's narration, on the first accepted perform (success, failure or performed); that perform also assigns the engine-owned player fact seen_tip_<key> (bool, default false) true, which the compiler adds, so a recipe with a tip has a key of at most 55 characters and no definition writes that fact (RESERVED_FACT). Optional (loka-j64e): reason, a text key the GameView adds as the message of an offered ActionSet action's (or learned spell word's) unavailable reason while its policy fails (a use-target recipe is hidden then, so its reason is not shown); the perform or cast refusal stays invalid_state. Optional (Homestead hs-10): craft (RecipeCraft), the items a station recipe uses up and makes; a spell recipe has none (SCHEMA_VIOLATION). Result bands join later.

anyOf.description: A luck roll (RecipeCheck).

A deterministic threshold (21 §7 Check: deterministic threshold, difficulty; R5 S6b), owned by check@1 like a luck roll: passes when the actor's body's current value of a resource of the cartridge, read at admission before the recipe's costs, is at least difficulty. It draws no RNG and emits check_passed or check_failed under key; the key rules of RecipeCheck apply.

An opposed check (toolbox rows 5 and G5, docs/system/mechanics.md): passes when the actor's level of skill, or value of attribute, at admission is at least the target detail's rating, or, when npc names an NPC of this cartridge (attribute only, toolbox row G3), that NPC's value of the attribute; draws no RNG. A skill with growth gains one use per perform.

A track check (toolbox row W13, docs/system/mechanics.md Tracks and trails): passes when the trail of population plan plan (its key; the plan declares trail) in the actor's room is fresh (world.trails.fresh_for); draws no RNG; on success the outcome's lines are followed by world.trails.leads[<exit>].

cues.description: Transient cues of this outcome (toolbox row G6), from the actor's room: perceived only by a cue_perceived condition of a reaction this outcome's check_passed, check_failed or action_completed causes; never stored or shown.

Transient cues of this outcome (toolbox row G6), from the actor's room: perceived only by a cue_perceived condition of a reaction this outcome's check_passed, check_failed or action_completed causes; never stored or shown.

source.BarrierDefinition.description: Shared mutable state for one logical door or gate (21 §5 Barrier), owned by barrier@1 (a cartridge with one requires it), keyed in CompiledCartridge.barriers by DefinitionRefString of kind barrier and named by the exits that pass through it (Connection.barrier): its key; keywords, the Alias words a player names it by after open, close, lock or unlock (the direction of its exit names it too); short, the text key of its short description ("the oak door"); initial, its state in a fresh world (BarrierState); and optionally key_item, the item whose holder may lock and unlock it (has_item: held directly or inside containers the holder holds). Without key_item no one can lock or unlock it. Damaged/repaired and blocked states join as optional fields. Optional tags are its property tags (entity.schema.json Tag, toolbox row G1).

opens_when.description: A condition its open command needs (toolbox row 10, barrier@1): while it fails, open is refused invalid_state; close, lock and unlock and an already open barrier are unaffected.

tags.description: Its property tags (Tag; toolbox row G1), read by the has_tag policy leaf (tags@1).

source.BleedDefinition.description: An authored body bleed duration, tick cadence and HP loss.

source.BlueprintDefinition.description: Built rooms S1 (construction@1; cartridge.md Blueprint and site declarations): one structure a player may build at a room's site (RoomDefinition.site). Its key; title and description, the text keys of the room it becomes; optional variants (DescriptionVariant) and tags (Tag) as a room's; optional locks.enter, the policy the mover must hold to come into the built room, as a room's (toolbox row G7). Nothing builds in S1: the cartridge declares and both compilers check. Built rooms S3: optional max_per_owner, the most rooms of this blueprint one character may own at once; an order at the cap is refused service.construction_full. Built rooms S4: optional weathering, a status of this cartridge the room gets when it is raised (and again when mended); optional ruin, the status a mend cures (a reaction applies it, typically on weathering's status_expired), the mend benefit refuses service.nothing_to_mend unless ruin is active on the room.

source.DialogueDefinition.description: One dialogue node (06 §17; Early R7/R8 D1), keyed in CompiledCartridge.dialogues by DefinitionRefString of kind dialogue, owned by dialogue@1 (a cartridge with one requires it): its key, also the stable action key of its talk (no action's, recipe's, quest's or registered command's: DUPLICATE_DEFINITION) and the beat of the choice it opens; npc, the speaker, whose talk the actor's ActionSet offers while the speaker is in the actor's room, and which is one of the npc roles (a speaker may have several dialogues: a talk to it opens the first, in key order, whose policy holds, and is invalid_state when none does); policy, the talk's availability, rechecked at Choose; prompt, the text key of the pending choice's prompt; roles, the participants talk binds to EntityIds in the durable choice (06 §33, §43: bound once, never re-resolved by name), each an npc that must be in the actor's room or an item the actor's body must hold when a choice is made (else not_present or not_owned), never named actor (the actor is always a participant: DUPLICATE_DEFINITION); quest, the quest a choice resolves through quest@1's resolution, with the choice_id as its outcome (absent in a dialogue with an accept choice, so accepting never resolves: OUTCOME_MISMATCH); and choices, at least one (a compiler check: the subset has no minProperties), each with its label, its narration line (committed with the actor's body and every role pinned), its fact.assign consequences and an optional hand_over of an item role to an npc role. Choices list in key order. API1.9 optionally adds riddle: its existing choice_id, lowercase canonical answer, ordered uppercase letter bank containing every answer letter with multiplicity, and wrong-answer narration text key.

keyword.description: Toolbox row G9 (speech@1): a say or whisper of this word to the speaker opens this dialogue, which talk never offers or opens; no riddle.

label.description: A distinct named Talk label opts that authored control into exact dialogue selection; omission retains first-eligible Talk.

source.ItemDefinition.description: A portable thing (21 §8): its key; keywords, the Alias words a player names it by (target resolution); short, the text key of its short description ("a brass lantern"); room_line, the text key of the line a room shows while it lies there ("A brass lantern sits here."), with room_line_variants (DescriptionVariant, first match wins, as for a room's description); description, the text key examine shows; location, where a fresh world puts it; and optionally container: true, making it a receptacle; only receptacles may declare capacity, the most items held directly (without capacity a receptacle has no limit); optionally slot, the SlotKey it is worn in (equipment@1), with optional affects (ItemAffect), each added to the wearer's attribute while the item is worn (toolbox row 3; needs slot and attributes@1); and optionally barrier, the barrier on it (a container's lid, barrier@1, c1-locks): a barrier of this cartridge that no exit and no other item names (BARRIER_MISMATCH), whose state the door verbs change with the item as target_id; while it is closed or locked, what the item holds is out of reach (containment@1 custody). Optional mass_grams is the shell mass, required for every item when world.carry is authored. Optional tags are its property tags (Tag, toolbox row G1). Optional short_variants and description_variants vary its short and description (TextVariants, toolbox row W6). Optional words are its name words (NameWords, loka-6qi).

container.description: Only explicitly authored receptacles hold items. Absence is false; capacity and barrier require this field.

equip.description: Authored wear and remove words (toolbox row 6a, loka-x6t.20): the Wear and Remove labels and the worn and removed lines. Only with slot; each key is in the text catalog.

give_allowed.description: API1.10: false prevents ordinary Give of this item or any container holding it transitively; absence permits Give when contents allow it. Dialogue hand_over remains legal.

identified.description: Toolbox row 27: a boolean fact, not per_subject; the item is identified while it reads true for the player, and GameView worn sums identified items only (needs affects).

immune.description: Toolbox row G3: statuses that status.apply skips on this item's instance; each names a declared status.

intended_level.description: Balance tool 6b: the level the item is meant for, read only by the power report's gear budget (needs affects; the engine ignores it at runtime).

locks.description: Toolbox row G7 (mechanics.md Access locks): at least one of get, the policy an actor must hold to take this item or anything inside it, and put, the policy to put an item into it (a container only: compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION invalid_value at locks.put). Each is read with this item as target; failing it refuses permission_denied.

mass_grams.description: The item shell mass in grams, excluding its contents. Required on every item under world.carry; explicit zero is valid (docs/system/cartridge.md Carrying settings and item mass).

tags.description: Its property tags (Tag; toolbox row G1), read by the has_tag policy leaf (tags@1).

source.LiquidDefinition.description: Cartridge-owned mass, integer serving and unit labels for a declared liquid.

cures.description: Statuses (toolbox rows 1 and G13) a Drink of this liquid ends; a service serving does not.

source.NpcDefinition.description: A non-player character (00a §4), as a holder of items so far: its key, keywords, short, room_line and description as for an item, the room a fresh world puts it in, and optionally capacity, the most items it holds. Optionally daily_schedule, its daily location schedule (schedule@1), and schedule_cases, its conditional hours (toolbox row W10); dialogue joins with its capability as an optional field. Optional hp opts into entity-specific HP (docs/system/cartridge.md NPC HP overrides). Optional short_variants, room_line_variants and description_variants vary its texts (TextVariants, toolbox row W6). Optional words are its name words (NameWords, loka-6qi).

ask.description: Toolbox row FD7 (speech@1 with topics@1): what the NPC says when asked about a topic. The first answer in authored order whose topic is the one asked and whose when holds (the player as the actor, the NPC as the target) is narrated and grants its grants topic; none: unknown.

attributes.description: Toolbox row G3: this NPC's base attribute values (attributes@1), read at use by an opposed check naming the NPC and by its derived attack; each names a distinct attribute of this cartridge. An attribute it does not list reads its definition start.

walks.description: Toolbox row W26 (mechanics.md NPCs use doors): the step moves only when a path to room exists through exits a walking NPC may cross (breadth first, direction-key order, one query step per exit); the NPC moves in one step, each locked door on the path it holds the key of is unlocked, opened, closed and locked again; no path leaves it where it is.

anyOf.description: Globally stable, immutable reference to a content definition (03 §2; 05 §4: no global content-key namespace). cartridge_id, kind and key are lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters; cartridge_version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata.

walks.description: Toolbox row W26 (mechanics.md NPCs use doors): the step moves only when a path to room exists through exits a walking NPC may cross (breadth first, direction-key order, one query step per exit); the NPC moves in one step, each locked door on the path it holds the key of is unlocked, opened, closed and locked again; no path leaves it where it is.

daily_schedule.description: schedule@1 (06 §13 Behavior/schedule profiles; 21 §10; capability_registry.json definitions): a daily location schedule. Each key is a nonnegative hour of the authored calendar day without a leading zero; the compiler checks it is below hours_per_day. From that hour until the next listed one (wrapping at day end) the NPC belongs in that room of this cartridge. A fresh world schedules one durable job at the first listed hour strictly after its start time; each job's run_job moves the NPC there, if it is elsewhere, and schedules the next (04 §5.4). Until its first job runs, the NPC stays in its room. An empty schedule schedules nothing.

disposition.description: Toolbox row G11: how the NPC stands toward the player, derived when read, never stored: hostile while hostile holds, else friendly while friendly holds, else wary (an NPC without it is wary). Each condition is read with the player as the actor and the NPC as the target, so subject target facts are its pair facts with the player. Hostile refuses talk and trade and, with an attack, engages a player who walks in, saying engage; friendly takes a friendly buy_discount. Toolbox row 35: with arrest instead of engage, a hostile NPC stops a player who walks in and the body goes to arrest.to, saying arrest.narration; no encounter opens.

refuse.description: Book hostile refusal: the line the Book shows on the NPC's page while it is hostile, naming the mood, never the cause; projected as its EntityView refusal.

drops.description: Toolbox row 8 loot table (docs/system/mechanics.md loot tables, world.death): in order, an item this NPC holds at genesis and its percent chance of passing to the corpse when combat kills the NPC; a failed item stays with the dead NPC.

immune.description: Toolbox row G3: statuses that status.apply skips on this NPC's instance; each names a declared status.

locks.description: Toolbox row 33 (mechanics.md Theft, fence and witnessed offense): get, the policy an actor must hold to take an item this NPC directly holds (target: that item); refuses permission_denied.

mount.description: Toolbox row 43b (needs world.mount): this NPC can be ridden. While world.mount.riding is true for (this NPC, a character) and both share a room, the character's moves need a destination room carrying one of terrain, each move's fare is scaled by cost_percent (default 100, floored, applied last) and this NPC moves with the body. Never on a spawn template.

source.PopulationBundle.description: One NPC, directly held item and public NPC corpse template for a bounded population.

source.PopulationPlan.description: One fixed-slot, two-room bounded population with an owned wander and replacement job.

birth_when.description: Toolbox row W12: while false at an occurrence, the plan births nothing above floor. Its tree may use only all, any, not, population_count, time_window, sky and barrier_state (SCHEMA_VIOLATION otherwise, from the compiler).

chance.description: Makes the plan an encounter plan (docs/system/mechanics.md Random encounters, toolbox row 9): each wander-boundary occurrence with an eligible slot draws one uniform(100) and a roll below chance births the first eligible slot. Absent: an RNG-free ecology plan.

floor.description: Toolbox row W12: slots 1 to floor refill at the plan's next occurrence: a member dying there is due at its death time, not after replacement_delay, and they birth whatever birth_when says. At most day_target; refused with chance (SCHEMA_VIOLATION, from the compiler).

hunts.description: Toolbox row W13: a member in a room holding a character's body holds; else each wander step takes the exit of the characters' fresh trail in the member's room when npcPassage admits it, else wanders as before; characters then leave trails (trail_exit, trail_at, instance scope); needs world.trails.

trail.description: Toolbox row W13 (mechanics.md Tracks and trails): a member's wander step and C4 flight write the room left's trail_<key>_exit and trail_<key>_at (engine facts, per room); needs world.trails.

walks.description: Toolbox row W26 (mechanics.md NPCs use doors): the wander step crosses its exit as a walking NPC does (npcPassage with walks): a closed door passes and stays closed, a locked one only for a member holding its key_item (unlocked, opened, closed and locked again); any traverse lock on the exit or enter lock on the room refuses it.

wander_when.description: Toolbox row W12: while false at a wander boundary, no member wanders. The same leaf limit as birth_when.

source.QuestDefinition.description: A quest with one objective (06 §2; R6P pre-release-proof.md), keyed in CompiledCartridge.quests by DefinitionRefString of kind quest, owned by quest@1 (a cartridge with one requires it): its key, also the stable action key of its offer (no action's, recipe's or registered command's: DUPLICATE_DEFINITION); title, the text key of its journal entry (QuestView.title); offer, optional, the accept action its actor's ActionSet lists while the actor has no instance of the quest (label its text key, policy its availability: while it fails the offer is shown unavailable and accept_quest is rejected), which resolves to accept_quest; without one, only a dialogue choice's accept (dialogue.schema.json DialogueChoice) activates the quest; and objective (QuestObjective). Resolution is another capability's: a choice resolves it through quest@1's resolution, which re-checks the objective. Giver, turn-in, prerequisites beyond the offer's policy, further objectives, outcomes and automatic or discovered activation join as optional fields. Optional journal declares lifecycle texts (QuestJournal); selection is computed in QuestView without changing persisted state.

deadline.description: A quest deadline, one object (validate.ts oneOf needs a const discriminator). Legacy (S2): at, fact, trust_fact and trust_amount, no after. Generic (toolbox row W24): exactly one of after (logical units from activation) or at (absolute logical time), no legacy field; activation schedules one engine job and expiry fails the instance with outcome and emits quest_failed. The compiler (lib/loka/content/quests.ex) refuses any other shape (SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

source.ReactionRule.description: Typed reaction owned by reaction@1. Every registered event kind can trigger; each optional filter must equal its payload field (W1). Every delivery runs for the command actor; quest resolution verifies the source instance; a status.apply hits the event's subject or its named item (docs/system/mechanics.md reaction@1). Apply may assign facts (an entity or pair fact, toolbox row W2, at its named npc's or item's instance, else at the event's subject when that is an NPC, item or detail; no subject, no write) or activate a quest on quest_resolved. API1.12 adds typed quest.resolve and quest.fail on fact_changed. Deliveries use one writer group and the existing FIFO budgets; faults commit nothing.

after.description: Toolbox row FD1: the steps run this many logical seconds after delivery, as a reaction job for the delivery's actor, when `when` holds at both times; due no earlier than 1 s after the proposal's clock.

with.description: Toolbox row FD4: an npc_pair fact's second NPC; the step writes at the pair (its subject toward this NPC).

anyOf.description: Toolbox row 15: adds amount to a bounded int fact, clamped to its minimum and maximum, at the subject a fact.assign step writes at.

with.description: Toolbox row FD4: an npc_pair fact's second NPC; the step writes at the pair (its subject toward this NPC).

anyOf.description: Suppress one authored population plan for duration logical seconds from this accepted fact-change cause, preserving current members and closing its current encounter.

Apply one authored status (toolbox row 1) at the cause's time to the event's subject (a body, NPC or thing, row G3), or to the named item's or (row 42, never with item; not a spawn template) NPC's authored instance, or (row W21, co_present) to every living NPC in the event's room; an active one is refreshed; an NPC or item that declares the status immune takes nothing.

co_present.description: Toolbox row W21: the status lands on every living NPC in the event's room (its room_id, else the room directly holding the subject; none for a carried or unplaced one), in EntityId order, never on the player's body; an NPC declaring the status immune takes nothing. Never with item or npc (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

room.description: Status reader 9: the status lands on this room of the cartridge, which holds it as any holder does (its tick changes nothing). Never with item, npc or co_present (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

tag.description: Toolbox row W22 (only with co_present): the status lands instead on every item lying directly in the event's room whose definition carries this tag, the event's subject included, in EntityId order; an item declaring the status immune takes nothing.

anyOf.description: Toolbox row W22 (Beads loka-kgd.96, barrier@1): move barrier, or every barrier on an exit of the event's room (its room_id, else the room directly holding the subject) whose definition carries tag, in direction-key order, to state to, from any state and with no key, opens_when or reach check (a burnt or broken door); each legal step on the way (locked, closed, open) is one barrier.transition and one barrier_changed, and a barrier already at to takes nothing. to locked needs the barrier's key_item, every tagged barrier's for tag (compiler BARRIER_UNREACHABLE_KEY at to).

Toolbox row G3 reader 3: end this status when active on the event's subject (the holder a status.apply without item, npc or co_present lands on), as a cure does: no event, no line. Once per holder and status in a rule, shared with status.apply: the first of the two steps on a pair wins.
Add amount experience to the acting character's levelling row (toolbox row 4), saturating at the ResourceInt maximum; needs world.levelling.

Toolbox row 41 (decay): when the event's subject is an item not already directly in room and not consumed, transfer it from its current holder to room (one entity.transfer, no event, no line, no capacity or reach check); any other subject takes nothing.

Toolbox row FD5 (loka-kgd.22): jumps the named NPC (else the event's subject when it is an NPC) to room, else the event's room, as a schedule move does (no exit, passage or lock), and emits entity_entered_room at the cause's time. Nothing when the NPC is dead, engaged, a following escort, blocked from moving or already there, no room resolves, or the delivery's character is in a running scene. Settle S4-1: plan (never with npc; room required) moves every living member of that population plan instead, in EntityId order, each as above.

Toolbox row 37a (phased world events): births one bundle of the population plan into its home, in the highest free slot up to cap, as the plan job's birth does; no free slot births nothing. No RNG draw (the plan's chance and targets govern its own job only).

Homestead hs-1: one run of the replenish entry key's move, as its job's run does (up to count of its items directly in from, lowest EntityId first, until to holds cap or is full), at once: no job completed or scheduled, no event, no line; nothing when nothing fits. Refused on a rule with after.

Settle S3-1: appends the authored line text to the delivery's narration, after the lines of the steps before it; no op, no event, no actor or subject read. Allowed with after: a fired rule's line joins its job's lines at the due time.
Toolbox row FD1: writes the delivery's logical time into an int fact (no maximum, minimum absent or at most 0) at the subject a fact.assign step writes at, as a fact.assign.

npc.description: The entrant is this NPC's authored instance (toolbox row W3).

anyOf.description: Toolbox row G9 (speech@1): one spoken event per NPC that heard the word.

npc.description: The hearer is this NPC's authored instance.

anyOf.description: Toolbox row FD7 (speech@1): the actor asked an NPC about a topic.

npc.description: The asked NPC is this NPC's authored instance.

witness.description: Toolbox row FD5: this NPC's authored instance, alive in the event subject's room, sees the subject (not blind, the subject not concealed from it); an event's subject is never its own witness.

attacker.description: The attacker is this NPC's authored instance (loka-kgd.79); a player's blow never matches.

target.description: The target is this NPC's authored instance (row 39); a blow on the player never matches.

witness.description: Toolbox row FD5: this NPC's authored instance, alive in the event subject's room, sees the subject (not blind, the subject not concealed from it); an event's subject is never its own witness.

anyOf.description: The world's hourly calendar event (toolbox row W25; schedule@1): no filters; a status lands on the actor's body.
Toolbox row G3 reader 2.

silent.description: Author-time only (mix loka.lint, pass-1 row 3): the rule writes state without a narrate step on purpose. The compiler drops it, so a compiled cartridge never carries it.

source.ReplenishPlan.description: One replenish entry (docs/system/cartridge.md Replenish declarations): each due job moves up to count of items, lowest EntityId first, from the holder from to the holder to until to holds cap of them, then schedules the next at its due time plus every. A move never exceeds to's declared capacity. The compiler (lib/loka/content/replenish.ex) refuses a template location, a holder with no placed entity (a spawn-template NPC or template item), an item holder that is not a container, an item to when any listed item is a container, from equal to to, duplicate items and an unresolved item or holder.

source.RoomDefinition.description: A navigable place (21 §5 Place/Room): its key, its title and description text keys (05 §18; resolved in the cartridge text catalog), and its exits by compass direction, the six-way compass of 00 §4.10 (a direction without an exit is absent), optionally its inspectable details by key, at most 64, its description variants (DescriptionVariant) and its contributions to the ActionSet of an actor in it, applied in order (action.schema.json ActionContribution; R5 S5, optional). Custom named connections (05 §17) join later as a separate optional field. Optional tags are its property tags (entity.schema.json Tag, toolbox row G1).

dark.description: The room is dark (light@1): a player without light, or blind, reads the engine line place.dark instead of the description and sees none of the room's entities. An authored dark_description wins over the engine line.

locks.description: Toolbox row G7 (mechanics.md Access locks): enter, the policy the mover must hold to come into this room, read by movementPlan after the exit's traverse lock; failing it refuses permission_denied. Read with no target.

site.description: Built rooms S1 (construction@1; cartridge.md Blueprint and site declarations): where a structure may be built from this room. directions, the compass directions a built room may open on, none an authored exit of this room (SITE_EXIT_CONFLICT); blueprints, the BlueprintDefinitions that may be built here (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE otherwise).

tags.description: Its property tags (Tag; toolbox row G1), read by the has_tag policy leaf (tags@1) and the terrain fare (row 43a); unique, since a repeated tag would apply its fare percent twice.

on.description: What starts the scene: a story point reached, a quest outcome, or an action recipe's success; an action start names the recipe's room and detail.

source.SceneDefinition.description: Modal narration or the consumed paid-Rest anchored, resumable presentation-only dream.

source.ServiceDefinition.description: Exact original-provider action and conserved quote with one typed immediate benefit.

price.description: Row kgd.70: 0 only on an entitlement with escrow, a barter.

source.SkillDefinition.description: An acquired skill with authored display text and a policy for current qualification.

growth.description: Toolbox row 5 (docs/system/mechanics.md skill growth): strictly increasing use counts reaching levels 2, 3 and so on above the base; the count is the reserved player fact uses_<key>.

hidden.description: Homestead hs-14 (docs/system/mechanics.md Skill trees): the skill is left out of GameView skills, and of NPC lessons, while its prerequisite fails and it is not acquired. A dialogue choice that teaches it is not offered while it is so left out. A non-hidden skill whose prerequisite or qualification reads a hidden skill, a dialogue policy that reads one, and a dialogue label on a dialogue that teaches one are refused.

prerequisite.description: Homestead hs-11 (docs/system/mechanics.md Skill trees): read for the acquiring actor with no target; skill.acquire is refused while it fails. A skill_compare naming this skill is refused.

profession.description: Homestead hs-14 (docs/system/book-ui.md Skill tree details): the profession heading this skill is listed under on the Character page.

source.StatusDefinition.description: Toolbox row 1: one authored timed status on a body. Every tick_every seconds until duration ends, per_tick (signed) is added to resource, saturating at the pool bounds; a negative hp result at zero runs the death sequence. Applied by a reaction status.apply; ended by expiry, an edible that cures it, or death. A reapplication while active refreshes ends_at and keeps the pending tick. Optional modifies (row 2c) adds attribute modifiers, read at use while active; a status with modifies may omit per_tick, and then never ticks (its one job is the expiry).

allows.description: Status reader 4: the only Command types the holding body may issue while the status is active (a modal answer aside); named as blocks; may stand in for per_tick.

blocks.description: Status reader 4: Command types (CommandPayload type) the holding body may not issue while the status is active; each names a registered command other than run_job and elapsed (compiler UNKNOWN_COMMAND); may stand in for per_tick.

concealment.description: Status reader 8: while active on an NPC, the player does not see it; on the player's body, an NPC does not engage it on entry. invisible yields to a see_invisible perception; hidden to none, unless pierced_by. May stand in for per_tick.

cues.description: Cues active while this status is active on a holder, from the holder's room (toolbox row G6).

duration.description: Logical seconds, or permanent (toolbox row W8): no expiry and no job, kept by the same-body return, ended only by a cure; a permanent status never ticks, so it declares no per_tick (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

fear.description: Toolbox row W21: while active on a pack member, its C4 flight is attempted on its every opponent turn, whatever its hp; may stand in for per_tick.

kind.description: Toolbox row loka-x6t.64: the status icon's polarity, shown as GameView ConditionView.kind; wins over the polarity derived from the effect fields.

modifies.description: Toolbox row 2c: while the status is active on a holder, each modifier is added to the holder's attribute as attributes@1 reads it.

movement.description: Status reader 7: the holding body's move cost and the terrain it may cross while the status is active; may stand in for per_tick.

cost_percent.description: Percent of each move's fare (world.movement.cost or 1 mv, after the flee multiplier) the holding body pays, rounded down; several statuses apply in turn in definition order.

passes.description: Terrain tags the holding body may enter: a move into a room tagged air, chasm or water is refused invalid_state unless the body's active statuses pass each such tag.

observed.description: Row G3 (loka-kgd.176): told when a first application lands on an NPC or item in the player's room that the player perceives, or on the room the player stands in (loka-x6t.37); with none, such a holder is silent.

skipped.description: Told, whole, when this status bars its holder's combat blow (loka-x6t.30); with none, the round tells the engine line combat.skipped, its bindings.status this status's label.

per_tick.description: Signed; never 0, required unless modifies, fear, blocks, allows, resistances, perception, concealment or movement is present or duration is permanent, and absent when duration is permanent (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION).

perception.description: Status reader 6: what the holding body perceives while the status is active. sight blind: every room is dark to it, a lit source or dark sight notwithstanding; dark_sight: sees in an unlit room as an ancestry's dark_sight does; see_invisible: sees a holder of an invisible status. hearing deaf: no sound cue reaches it. At least one field (compiler SCHEMA_VIOLATION); may stand in for per_tick.

pierced_by.description: Toolbox row 16, only beside concealment: a seer whose attribute value (an NPC's declared value, a player's attributes@1 value) is greater than the holder's skill level sees through the concealment; a holder without a character is never pierced. No draw. While the holder is a player's body, an NPC that engages it on entry ends every active concealment status on it.

resistances.description: Status reader 5: while active on the struck body (the player's or an NPC's), each entry joins the G2 resistance sum of an attack on it, before the one -100..100 clamp; may stand in for per_tick.

source.StoryPointDefinition.description: A story point the cartridge declares (23 §3; 03 §26; Early R7/R8 D2), keyed in CompiledCartridge.story_points by DefinitionRefString of kind story_point, its event story_point_reached owned by dialogue@1: its key, the report's story point (account.schema.json StoryPointReport), and outcomes, at least one (a compiler check: the subset has no minProperties), each reached by its rule-owned trigger: the choice of a dialogue (choose emits story_point_reached after choice_resolved in that decision's root sequence). A trigger site feeds one outcome of one story point (DUPLICATE_DEFINITION), and its dialogue resolves a quest (OUTCOME_MISMATCH otherwise), so a choice reaches it once. In source it is story_points/<key>.json, its dialogue a short reference.

source.TopicDefinition.description: A declared localized topic mapped to its player Boolean knowledge fact.

source.TransportDefinition.description: Paired original boarding detail, destination, conserved fare recipient and corpse recovery rooms.

source.VersionedPolicy.description: A policy tree with the AST version it was written against (14 §R3A 'core policy AST/versioning'). A new leaf operator is versioned by its owning capability, which the cartridge must lock (capability_registry.json policies); adding an operator to a capability version that is already installed takes that capability's next version. A changed meaning of an existing operator takes a new policy_version.

source.cartridge.description: A cartridge's manifest (05 §3, §20): identity, title, compatibility requirements and supported profiles (at least one; order and duplicates carry no meaning). Fields that freeze with their feature (entry, locales, activation groups, continuity, time policy) are added then (14 §R3B).

alternates.description: Narration variety (variety@1, toolbox row W7): a text key's alternates, each a key of the text catalog; a committed narration line with that key shows one of the key and its alternates, chosen by a hash of the command id and the key (mechanics.md narration variety), never the authority RNG.

ancestries.description: Authored once-only character choices (attributes@1), keyed by choice Key.

chapters.description: Optional ordered chapter markers; absent preserves earlier cartridge bytes and meaning.

speech.description: Word bar S2 (speech@1): phrases, the cartridge's static say words, each a speech@1 Word, offered to every actor with no fact gate; GameView projects them as phrases. In source it is cartridge.json's speech, beside world.

additionalProperties.description: A typed, namespaced fact declaration (03 §7): key (the fact's DefinitionRef is cartridge@version:fact/key; the cartridge is the namespace, 05 §4), versioned type, default, allowed scope kinds (a set) and meaning. Transition constraints and the reference graph are added with the compiler (R4).

npc_pair.description: Toolbox row FD4: a pair fact between two NPCs, one value per ordered pair (the subject NPC toward the with NPC), stored with subject_id and with_id. Needs per_subject and scopes exactly [instance] (world state).

per_subject.description: Toolbox row W2: the fact has one value per subject, an NPC, item or detail, stored with its subject_id (ScopedFact): an entity fact at scope instance, a pair fact (the subject and the character) at scope player. Absent: one value per scope.
